summary: Full published-paper reading and a section-by-section mathematical inventory, with explicit genericity/convention boundaries and source corrections. The routing closes the inventory but does not yet certify proof-input closure, split every bundled conclusion or finish each definition API; the extraction remains partial for the listed gaps. Continuation codex-hjdg0j adds 14 items separating Elkik precision, complete-local domains and affinoid connectedness, including two exact library atoms; adds the analytic product source route and one adjacent-source cross-reference correction. A further codex-7e92bd continuation adds Z15–Z24 and five exact library atoms, exposes the general-DVR saturated-jet proof, and removes its apparent dependency on the narrower arithmetic theorem. Analytic and remaining regular-structure atom closure stay explicit. Continuation codex-a71f92 audits the precise completion/regular-coordinate suppliers: imports sixteen pinned library theorem atoms, exposes five elementary adapters, and coalesces local regularity/dimension under completion with existing ModularCurves §4D. The overall extraction and implementation remain partial. Newton continuation: Z30–Z39 separate Taylor error, differentiated conductor identities, weighted adjugates, cancellation, witness stability, quantitative congruence limits and base-change inclusion; L24–L33 are exact pinned imports. Z03 has six typed tests. Smooth-locus supplier closure and the other recorded gaps remain; status stays partial. Second codex-a71f92 continuation adds L34–L49 and Z40–Z44: fixed-presentation conductor witnesses, both directions of the smooth-locus criterion and a universal radical-power identity, with exact pinned suppliers. The Noetherian convention in Elkik is distinguished from the separately proved finite-presentation extension; Z07 retains its strict m>r evaluation threshold. The overall extraction is still partial. Analytic continuation by codex-7e92bd adds L50–L60/Z45–Z62: pointed connectedness without normality, strict-affinoid normalization/Nullstellensatz and rational fibers, finite scalar comparison, and finite-type integral completion flatness. The regularity argument is decomposed with exact remaining G-ring and regular-local supplier gaps. Status remains partial. Codex-c83e7a continuation adds24 items (480 total): K45–K48 close the generic tame-to-semisimple adapter; A25–A33 expose exact prime/generator, polarized adequacy and projected-level interfaces; G38–G44 specify monodromy recurrence/precision; Z63–Z66 decompose the regular-local domain argument. E36–E38 are three new unreviewed findings. Status remains partial; the ten gap records specify the remaining work. Continuation cc-442dc5 (Claude Code) supplies itemwise uses, API outlines and typed unit tests for the thirty §2 definitions and constructions that lacked them (Weyl-group, genericity, Serre-weight, Deligne–Lusztig, tame-type and Weil–Deligne notions), from a fresh reading of published PDF24–53; the remaining definition/construction API census and the other listed gaps stay open, and the status remains partial.

items.name: Coefficient, root and Frobenius conventions
items.statement: Fix p, sufficiently large E/Qp, its integers O, uniformizer varpi and residue F. For the applications G=GLn and Op finite etale over Zp; J=Hom(Op,O), Gbold=Res(Op/Zp)G base changed to O, pi(lambda)_sigma=lambda_(sigma Frobenius^-1). Use eta=(n-1,...,0) in each embedding, h_lambda=max over all roots of <lambda,alpha^vee>, X0 the characters pairing zero with every root. HT(cyclotomic)=+1 and covariant period functors; filtration jumps have opposite signs. General root statements retain the split connected reductive setup and existence of eta specified in §1.8.1.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: η fixes lowest-alcove presentations F(π⁻¹(w̃₁)·(ω−η)) of Serre weights (PDF37).
π and F* = pπ⁻¹ define the tame parameters τ(w,μ) (PDF45).
Serre weights are parametrized by X₁(T)/(p−π)X⁰(T) (PDF35).
The convention HT(ε) = +1 fixes the order of the diagonal Hodge–Tate weights (see E20).

api.name: LLHLM.eta_pairing_simple
api.statement: ⟨η, α^∨⟩ = 1 for every simple root α; for G = GL_n^J, η = (n−1, …, 0) in every embedding and η is π-invariant.

api.name: LLHLM.frobeniusTwist_apply
api.statement: π(λ)_σ = λ_{σ∘φ⁻¹}; with σ_j = σ₀∘φ^{−j} this reads π(λ)_j = λ_{j+1}, so π⁻¹ shifts the embedding index by −1.

api.name: LLHLM.hBound_def
api.statement: h_λ = max_{α∈Φ} ⟨λ, α^∨⟩; for GL_n this is max_{i,j}(λ_i − λ_j) in each embedding, and h_λ = 0 iff λ ∈ X⁰(T) when Φ ≠ ∅.

api.name: LLHLM.X0_eq
api.statement: X⁰(T) = {λ : ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ = 0 for all α ∈ Φ}; for GL_n^J it is (Z·(1,…,1))^J.

api.name: LLHLM.HT_cyclotomic
api.statement: HT_κ(ε) = {1} for every κ, with covariant D_dR, D_pst, D_pcris; the Hodge filtration jumps sit at the negatives of the Hodge–Tate weights.

tests.name: LLHLM.hBound_eta_GL3
tests.statement: For GL₃ with η = (2,1,0), h_η = 2.

tests.name: LLHLM.X0_torus
tests.statement: If G = T is a torus (no roots), X⁰(T) = X*(T).

tests.name: LLHLM.frobeniusTwist_f1
tests.statement: If f = 1 (J a singleton), π is the identity on X*(T).

tests.name: LLHLM.HT_sign
tests.statement: The cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight +1 here; the opposite convention of [14, 22] (weight −1) must not be used.

items.name: Extended affine Weyl datum
items.statement: Wa=root lattice semidirect W and Wtilde=X*(T) semidirect W act on V=X*(T) tensor R. A0 has 0<root-pairing<1 for every positive root. Omega=Stab(A0), Wtilde=Wa semidirect Omega. Wplus sends A0 into the dominant chamber, W1plus into a restricted alcove (simple-root pairings between0 and1); wh=w0 t_-eta. Retain the central directions of the apartment.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: W̃₁⁺ and W̃⁺ are the factors of admissible pairs (2.2).
Regular elements factor as w̃₂⁻¹w₀t_νw̃₁ with w̃ᵢ ∈ W̃₁⁺ (Proposition 2.1.5).
Presentations of a Serre weight form an Ω-orbit (Lemma 2.2.4 proof).
w̃_h = w₀t_{−η} defines Herzig's involution R.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.translation_mul
api.statement: t_ν t_ν′ = t_{ν+ν′} and w t_ν w⁻¹ = t_{w(ν)}; W̃ = X*(T) ⋊ W and W_a = ZΦ ⋊ W.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.affine_omega_semidirect
api.statement: W̃ = W_a ⋊ Ω with Ω = Stab_{W̃}(A₀); W_a acts simply transitively on alcoves.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.quotient_affine_equiv
api.statement: W̃/W_a ≅ Ω ≅ X*(T)/ZΦ ≅ X*(Z), sending t_ν w to ν|_Z.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.mem_dominant_iff
api.statement: w̃ ∈ W̃⁺ iff w̃(A₀) is dominant, and w̃ ∈ W̃₁⁺ iff moreover 0 < ⟨x, α^∨⟩ < 1 on w̃(A₀) for every simple α; W̃₁⁺ ⊂ W̃⁺ and both are stable under right multiplication by Ω.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.wh_mem
api.statement: w̃_h = w₀ t_{−η} lies in W̃₁⁺.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_noncommute
tests.statement: For GL₂ with s the transposition, s t_{(1,0)} = t_{(0,1)} s ≠ t_{(1,0)} s.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_omega
tests.statement: For GL₂, δ = t_{(1,0)}s maps A₀ = {0 < x₁−x₂ < 1} to itself, Ω = ⟨δ⟩ ≅ Z and δ² = t_{(1,1)}.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.torus
tests.statement: If G = T is a torus, W_a = 1 and Ω = W̃ = X*(T).

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.w0_not_dominant
tests.statement: For GL₂, s ∉ W̃⁺ (it sends A₀ to the antidominant chamber), whereas w̃_h = s t_{(−1,0)} sends A₀ to A₀.

items.name: Length, Bruhat and upper-arrow orders
items.statement: Extend affine Coxeter length by l(w delta)=l(w), delta in Omega. Bruhat and Jantzen upper-arrow orders compare w1 delta and w2 delta exactly when their Wa parts compare; distinct right Wa cosets are incomparable. A relation X<=Y or X upward Y between sets means all pairs compare. Define W_le_z={x:x<=z}. Upper-arrow is not silently identified with Bruhat outside its comparison theorem's hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Wang's theorem compares ↑ and ≤ on W̃⁺ (Proposition 2.1.6, PDF31–32).
The upper-arrow relation defines admissible pairs.
Covering is tested by an upper-arrow inequality (Proposition 2.3.12(2)).
Closure relations among affine Schubert cells use the Bruhat order (Theorem 4.2.4).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.length_mul_omega
api.statement: ℓ(w δ) = ℓ(w) for w ∈ W_a and δ ∈ Ω; in particular ℓ(δ) = 0.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.le_iff_sameCoset
api.statement: w₁δ ≤ w₂δ′ iff δ = δ′ and w₁ ≤ w₂ in W_a; elements of different right W_a-cosets are incomparable. The same holds for ↑.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.upArrow_X0
api.statement: The relation ↑ is stable under simultaneous left translation by t_ν, ν ∈ X⁰(T) ([47, II.6.5(4)]).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.upArrow_iff_le_dominant
api.statement: For w̃₁, w̃₂ ∈ W̃⁺, w̃₁ ↑ w̃₂ iff w̃₁ ≤ w̃₂ (Wang's theorem [83, Theorem 4.3]; [56, Theorem 4.1.1]), as used on PDF32.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.lowerSet_def
api.statement: W̃^{≤z} := {x : x ≤ z}, a lower set of the Bruhat order.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_central_incomparable
tests.statement: For GL₂, ℓ(t_{(1,1)}) = 0 and t_{(1,1)} is incomparable with 1, because they lie in different W_a-cosets.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_lowerSet
tests.statement: For GL₂, W̃^{≤t_{(1,0)}} = {t_{(1,0)}, δ} with δ = t_{(1,0)}s of length 0.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.bruhat_not_length
tests.statement: For GL₂, t_{(1,0)} and t_{(0,1)} both have length 1 and lie in one W_a-coset, but neither is ≤ the other.

items.name: Reduced products of affine elements
items.statement: For m>=1 and w1,...,wm in Wtilde, the displayed product is reduced when l(product wi)=sum l(wi); factors need not be simple reflections.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: w̃₂⁻¹w₀w̃₁ is a reduced product for w̃₁, w̃₂ ∈ W̃₁⁺ (Lemma 2.1.4).
Reducedness transfers Bruhat inequalities in the proof of Proposition 2.1.6.
(−)* preserves reduced expressions in §4.3 (PDF89–90).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsReducedProd_iff
api.statement: w̃₁⋯w̃ₘ is reduced iff ℓ(w̃₁⋯w̃ₘ) = Σᵢ ℓ(w̃ᵢ).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.length_mul_le
api.statement: ℓ(xy) ≤ ℓ(x) + ℓ(y), so a reduced product has maximal length.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsReducedProd.sub
api.statement: Any consecutive sub-product of a reduced product is reduced, and a regrouping of a reduced product is reduced.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsReducedProd.omega
api.statement: Replacing (w̃ᵢ, w̃ᵢ₊₁) by (w̃ᵢδ, δ⁻¹w̃ᵢ₊₁) with δ ∈ Ω preserves reducedness.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsReducedProd.star
api.statement: If w̃₁⋯w̃ₘ is reduced, so is w̃ₘ*⋯w̃₁* in W̃^∨ ([56, Lemma 2.1.3]).

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.reduced_single
tests.statement: A product with one factor (m = 1) is reduced.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_ss_not_reduced
tests.statement: For GL₂, s·s = 1 is not reduced: 0 < 1 + 1.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_opposed_translations
tests.statement: For GL₂, t_{(1,0)}·t_{(0,1)} = t_{(1,1)} is not reduced: ℓ = 0 < 2.

items.name: Admissible set
items.statement: Adm(lambda)=union over finite Weyl w of {z:z<=t_(w lambda)} for lambda in X*(T).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Membership in Adm(λ+η) is one side of Proposition 2.1.6.
Constituents of R̄⊗W(λ) are cut out by t_ω W̃_{≤w₀w̃₁} ⊂ t_μ s Adm(λ+η) (Proposition 2.3.8).
Adm^reg(λ) labels the top-dimensional components of the naive special fibre (Corollary 4.2.6, PDF84).
A nonzero tame deformation ring forces w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η) (Corollary 5.5.8).
Admissibility of w̃(ρ̄,τ) yields an obvious common weight (Proposition 2.6.6).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.mem_adm_iff
api.statement: z ∈ Adm(λ) iff z ≤ t_{w(λ)} for some w ∈ W.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.translation_mem_adm
api.statement: t_{w(λ)} ∈ Adm(λ) for every w ∈ W.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_lowerSet
api.statement: Adm(λ) is a lower set: z′ ≤ z ∈ Adm(λ) implies z′ ∈ Adm(λ).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_weyl_invariant
api.statement: Adm(w(λ)) = Adm(λ) for w ∈ W.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_coset
api.statement: Every element of Adm(λ) lies in the W_a-coset of t_λ, whose class in W̃/W_a ≅ X*(Z) is λ|_Z.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_pi
api.statement: For G = G^J with the componentwise order, Adm(λ) = ∏_j Adm(λ_j) (PDF94).

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_central
tests.statement: If λ ∈ X⁰(T), then t_λ ∈ Ω and Adm(λ) = {t_λ}.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_not_single_interval
tests.statement: For GL₂, t_{(0,1)} ∈ Adm((1,0)) but t_{(0,1)} ≰ t_{(1,0)}; the union over W is necessary.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.adm_product
tests.statement: For GL₂^J, Adm((1,0)^J) has 3^{|J|} elements.

items.name: Regular alcoves and regular admissible elements
items.statement: The alpha-strip of index m is m< <x,alpha^vee> <m+1. An alcove is regular if it is contained in no positive-root critical strip of index0. An affine element is regular when its image of A0 is regular; Admreg(lambda) is the regular part of Adm(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Regular elements factor through W̃₁⁺ (Proposition 2.1.5).
Adm^reg(λ+η) is in bijection with AP(λ+η) (Corollary 2.1.7).
Regular admissible elements label translated top components (Theorem 4.3.10, PDF92).
Adm^reg(η) with its Remark 2.1.8 factorization enters §8.6 (PDF178).

api.name: Alcove.IsRegular_iff
api.statement: An alcove A is regular iff for every positive root α, A ⊄ H_α^{(0,1)} = {0 < ⟨x, α^∨⟩ < 1}.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsRegular_def
api.statement: w̃ is regular iff w̃(A₀) is regular; Adm^reg(λ) := {w̃ ∈ Adm(λ) : w̃ regular}.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.isRegular_mul_omega
api.statement: w̃δ is regular iff w̃ is, for δ ∈ Ω, since δ(A₀) = A₀.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.isRegular_iff_factor
api.statement: w̃ is regular iff w̃ = w̃₂⁻¹w₀t_νw̃₁ with w̃₁, w̃₂ ∈ W̃₁⁺ and ν dominant, unique up to X⁰(T) (Proposition 2.1.5).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.admReg_equiv_AP
api.statement: Adm^reg(λ+η) ≃ AP(λ+η) via (w̃₁, w̃₂) ↦ w̃₂⁻¹w₀w̃₁ (Corollary 2.1.7).

tests.name: Alcove.base_not_regular
tests.statement: A₀ lies in every critical strip, so 1 and every δ ∈ Ω are not regular.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_admReg_eta
tests.statement: For GL₂ with η = (1,0), Adm^reg(η) = {t_{(1,0)}, t_{(0,1)}}: the length-zero element t_{(1,0)}s of Adm(η) is not regular.

tests.name: Alcove.strip_not_wall
tests.statement: For GL₂, the alcove {−1 < x₁−x₂ < 0} is regular: it lies in the α-strip of index −1, not in the critical strip.

items.name: Opposed dominant factors are reduced
items.statement: For w1,w2 in Wplus, w2^-1 w0 w1 is a reduced product.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular affine-element factorization
items.statement: Every regular affine element is w2^-1 w0 t_nu w1 for w1,w2 in W1plus and dominant nu; the data are unique up to the central X0 action described in the proof.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Converse regularity
items.statement: For any w1,w2 in Wplus, w2^-1 w0 w1 is regular.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility and upper-arrow criterion
items.statement: For dominant lambda and w1,w2 in Wplus, the following are equivalent: w1 upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2; w2 upward wh t_-lambda w1; z=w2^-1 w0 w1 lies below BOTH t_(barw1^-1(lambda+eta)) and t_((w0 barw2)^-1(lambda+eta)); z belongs to Adm(lambda+eta). Bars mean finite Weyl images. This item needs separation into four implication leaves at blueprint time.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible pairs
items.statement: AP(lambda+eta) consists of pairs (w1,w2) in W1plus times Wplus modulo the diagonal central X0 action, satisfying w1 upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2, for dominant lambda.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: AP(λ+η) ≃ Adm^reg(λ+η) (Corollary 2.1.7).
AP(λ+η) parametrizes JH(R̄⊗W(λ)) via (2.8) (Proposition 2.3.7).
AP(λ) labels the d-dimensional components of M^nv(≤λ,∇_a)_F (Theorem 4.3.10, PDF92).
Unique admissible pairs attach Serre weights to components (PDF95–96).

api.name: AdmissiblePair.mem_iff
api.statement: (w̃₁, w̃₂) ∈ AP(λ+η) iff w̃₁ ∈ W̃₁⁺, w̃₂ ∈ W̃⁺ and w̃₁ ↑ t_λ w̃_h⁻¹ w̃₂, taken modulo the diagonal X⁰(T)-action.

api.name: AdmissiblePair.diag_X0
api.statement: The defining relation is invariant under (w̃₁, w̃₂) ↦ (t_νw̃₁, t_νw̃₂), ν ∈ X⁰(T), so AP(λ+η) is well defined.

api.name: AdmissiblePair.iff_adm
api.statement: w̃₁ ↑ t_λw̃_h⁻¹w̃₂ iff w̃₂⁻¹w₀w̃₁ ∈ Adm(λ+η) (Proposition 2.1.6).

api.name: AdmissiblePair.equiv_admReg
api.statement: (w̃₁, w̃₂) ↦ w̃₂⁻¹w₀w̃₁ is a bijection AP(λ+η) ≃ Adm^reg(λ+η).

api.name: AdmissiblePair.equiv_JH
api.statement: For R with an m-generic presentation, m ≥ max{2h_η, h_{λ+η}}, (w̃₁, w̃₂) ↦ F_{(w̃₁, w̃(R)w̃₂⁻¹(0))} is a bijection onto JH(R̄⊗W(λ)) (Proposition 2.3.7).

tests.name: AdmissiblePair.GL2_eta
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = 0, AP(η) has 2 elements, matching |Adm^reg(η)| = 2 = |W|.

tests.name: AdmissiblePair.GL2_std
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = (1,0), AP(λ+η) has 4 elements, matching the four constituents of R̄⊗Std for generic principal-series R.

tests.name: AdmissiblePair.not_single_translate
tests.statement: Translating only one coordinate by ν ∈ X⁰(T)∖{0} changes the W_a-coset of t_λw̃_h⁻¹w̃₂; the pair then fails the ↑ condition. Only the diagonal action is quotiented.

tests.name: AdmissiblePair.outer_reflexive
tests.statement: For every w̃₁, the pair (w̃₁, w̃_ht_{−λ}w̃₁) satisfies the ↑ condition with equality, since t_λw̃_h⁻¹w̃_ht_{−λ}w̃₁ = w̃₁.

items.name: Admissible-pair parametrization
items.statement: For dominant lambda, (w1,w2) maps to w2^-1 w0 w1 and gives a bijection AP(lambda+eta) -> Admreg(lambda+eta).
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reversed restricted-factor parametrization
items.statement: The same bijection holds for pairs in Wplus times W1plus modulo X0 with the same upper-arrow relation; the formula for the affine element is unchanged.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dual affine opposition map
items.statement: The target Wtilde-dual has the same group law but Bruhat order based at the antidominant alcove. Define (t_nu w)^*=w^-1 t_nu. It is an order equivalence and reverses products: (xy)^*=y^*x^*. The printed group-isomorphism assertion needs correction E1; use the opposite group for a multiplicative equivalence.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The cells S°_F(w̃*) ∩ Fl^{∇_a} are indexed through (−)* (Theorem 4.2.4, PDF83–84).
Top components are closures of S°_F(w̃₁*w₀w̃₂⁻¹*)-type cells (PDF89–92).
Smallness is preserved by (−)* (Proposition 2.1.12(3)).
§8 uses the star to move between W̃ and W̃^∨ labels (PDF166, 170).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_apply
api.statement: (t_ν w)* = w⁻¹ t_ν ∈ W̃^∨.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_mul
api.statement: (xy)* = y*x*; (−)* is a group isomorphism W̃ ≅ (W̃^∨)^op, not W̃ ≅ W̃^∨ (E1).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_star
api.statement: Applying the same formula twice returns x: (x*)* = x.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_le_iff
api.statement: x ≤ y in W̃ iff x* ≤ y* in W̃^∨ with the antidominant-alcove Bruhat order ([56, Lemma 2.1.3]).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.length_star
api.statement: ℓ(x*) = ℓ(x), and (−)* reverses reduced expressions.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_GL2_antimult
tests.statement: For GL₂, (t_{(1,0)}s)* = s t_{(1,0)} = s*·t_{(1,0)}*, whereas t_{(1,0)}*·s* = t_{(1,0)}s ≠ s t_{(1,0)}; so (−)* is not multiplicative.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_finite
tests.statement: On W ⊂ W̃, (−)* is inversion w ↦ w⁻¹; on translations it is the identity t_ν ↦ t_ν.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.star_involutive
tests.statement: For every x ∈ W̃, (x*)* = x.

items.name: Alcove depth
items.statement: A weight lambda is m-deep in an eta-shifted p-alcove with strip indices n_alpha if n_alpha p+m < <lambda+eta,alpha^vee> < (n_alpha+1)p-m. For m>=0, being m-deep in some alcove is equivalent to m<abs(<lambda+eta,alpha^vee>+pk) for all positive roots alpha and integers k.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Constituent depth bounds are stated in m-depth (Lemma 2.2.1).
JH(R̄⊗W(λ)) consists of (m−h_{λ+η})-deep weights (Proposition 2.3.7).
m-generic tame types require μ to be m-deep in C₀ (Definition 2.4.3).
Depth hypotheses such as 4n-deep weights enter §7.4 (PDF159).

api.name: Weight.IsDeepIn_def
api.statement: λ is m-deep in the η-shifted p-alcove with strip indices (n_α) iff n_αp + m < ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ < (n_α+1)p − m for all α ∈ Φ⁺.

api.name: Weight.isDeep_iff
api.statement: For m ≥ 0, λ is m-deep in some alcove iff m < |⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ + pk| for all α ∈ Φ⁺ and k ∈ Z.

api.name: Weight.IsDeep.mono
api.statement: If m′ ≤ m, m-deep implies m′-deep.

api.name: Weight.IsDeep.dotAct
api.statement: Depth is preserved by the p-dot action of W̃ (Remark 2.1.11(1)).

api.name: Weight.IsDeep.add
api.statement: If λ is m-deep and |⟨ν, α^∨⟩| ≤ k for all α, then λ+ν is (m−k)-deep.

tests.name: Weight.GL2_depth
tests.statement: For GL₂, p = 7 and λ = (3,0), ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ = 4, so λ is 2-deep in C₀ but not 3-deep.

tests.name: Weight.zero_deep_wall
tests.statement: λ is 0-deep iff ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ ∉ pZ for all α; for GL₂ and p = 7, λ = (6,0) is not 0-deep.

tests.name: Weight.eta_shift
tests.statement: For GL₂, λ = (−1,0) has ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ = −1 ∉ pZ but ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ = 0, so it is not 0-deep; depth is measured after the η-shift.

tests.name: Weight.depth_central
tests.statement: Depth is invariant under λ ↦ λ+ν for ν ∈ X⁰(T).

items.name: Affine genericity and smallness
items.statement: For z=w t_nu in either affine group, m-generic means nu-eta is m-deep, and m-small means h_nu<=m. Keep this right-translation convention; converting t_nu w uses the finite Weyl action.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 4.2.4 assumes w̃ is h-small (Definition 2.1.10(3), PDF83).
Genericity and smallness of translations are W-invariant (Proposition 2.1.12(1)).
A small factor loses a bounded amount of genericity (Proposition 2.1.12(4)).
t_ω is assumed (n−1)-generic (Definition 2.1.10(2), PDF91).
Generic presentations of τ make w̃(τ) generic (PDF105, 122).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsGeneric_def
api.statement: w t_ν (in W̃ or W̃^∨) is m-generic iff ν − η is m-deep.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsSmall_def
api.statement: w t_ν is m-small iff h_ν ≤ m, i.e. ⟨ν, α^∨⟩ ≤ m for all α ∈ Φ.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.isGeneric_translation_weyl
api.statement: t_ν is m-generic (resp. m-small) iff t_{s(ν)} is, for all s ∈ W.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsSmall.mul
api.statement: If w̃ is m-small and z̃ is m′-small, then w̃z̃ is (m+m′)-small.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.isSmall_inv_star
api.statement: w̃ is m-small iff w̃⁻¹ is iff w̃* is.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.IsGeneric.mul_small
api.statement: If z̃ is m′-generic, w̃ is m-small and m ≤ m′, then z̃w̃ is (m′−m)-generic.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL2_generic
tests.statement: For GL₂ and p = 7, t_{(3,0)} is 2-generic but not 3-generic, since ⟨(3,0), α^∨⟩ = 3.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.identity_small_not_generic
tests.statement: The identity is 0-small but not 0-generic.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.small_not_generic
tests.statement: Smallness does not imply genericity: t_{(1,0)} is 1-small for GL₂, but it is not 1-generic for any p, since ⟨(1,0), α^∨⟩ = 1.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.GL_small
tests.statement: For GL_n, t_ν is m-small iff max_i ν_i − min_i ν_i ≤ m in each embedding.

items.name: Polynomial genericity
items.statement: For P in Z[X1,...,Xn] and a in R^n, P-generic means P(a) modulo p is a unit in R/p. For a tuple indexed by finite J require this in every factor. This condition is generally not preserved by Weyl or dot actions.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: P-generic μ yields the local-model diagram of Theorem 7.3.2(2) (PDF151).
The weight part of Serre's conjecture is proved for P-generic lowest-alcove presentations (Theorem 9.1.6, PDF184).
The shifted polynomial genericity (8.1) is built from Definition 2.1.10(4).
Appendix B's explicit genericity polynomial (Corollary B.0.5; see E26).

api.name: PolyGeneric_def
api.statement: a ∈ Rⁿ is P-generic iff the image of P(a) in R/p is a unit; a ∈ (Rⁿ)^J is P-generic iff each a_j is.

api.name: PolyGeneric.mul_iff
api.statement: a is PQ-generic iff it is P-generic and Q-generic.

api.name: PolyGeneric.map
api.statement: If f : R → S is a ring map and a is P-generic, then f(a) is P-generic.

api.name: PolyGeneric.Pm_iff_deep
api.statement: For G = GL_n^J and λ−η ∈ C₀, λ is P_m-generic iff λ−η is m-deep, with P_m = ∏_{i=1}^n ∏_{j=1}^m (X_i − X_{i+1} − j) and X_{n+1} = X₁ (Remark 2.1.11(2)).

tests.name: PolyGeneric.one
tests.statement: Every tuple is 1-generic; over R = Z_p no tuple is p-generic.

tests.name: PolyGeneric.GL2_P1
tests.statement: For p = 7 and λ = (3,0), P₁(λ) = (3−0−1)(0−3−1) = −8 ≡ 6 mod 7, a unit; consistently, λ−η = (2,0) is 1-deep in C₀.

tests.name: PolyGeneric.not_weyl_invariant
tests.statement: For P = X₁ − X₂ − 1, (1,0) is not P-generic but (0,1) is, for p ≠ 2; P-genericity is not W-invariant (Remark 2.1.11(1)).

items.name: Genericity and smallness transport
items.statement: For nu a weight and every finite Weyl s, t_nu is m-generic (respectively m-small) iff t_(s nu) is; depth is invariant under the p-dot action and smallness under the ordinary Weyl action.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness under products
items.statement: If w is m-small and z is m'-small then wz is (m+m')-small, in either affine group.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness under inversion and opposition
items.statement: w is m-small iff w^-1 is m-small iff w^* is m-small.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Loss of genericity under a small factor
items.statement: If z is m'-generic and w is m-small with m<=m', then zw is (m'-m)-generic.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral highest-weight and virtual Weyl modules
items.statement: For dominant lambda, W(lambda)_O=Ind_B^G(w0 lambda), its E fibre is irreducible of highest weight lambda, and L(lambda) is the socle of its F fibre. For arbitrary lambda use the alternating derived-induction class sum_i(-1)^i R^i Ind_B^G(w0 lambda). V(lambda) is the restriction of the E module to G0(Zp), and W(lambda) the restriction of the F module to G0(Fp); distinguish genuine modules from virtual classes.
items.note: Route owner: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: JH(R̄⊗W(λ)) is parametrized by admissible pairs (Proposition 2.3.7).
Constituents of W(μ) have bounded depth (Lemma 2.2.1).
σ(λ,τ) = W(λ)⊗σ(τ) enters Breuil–Mézard patching (PDF169, 176).
Patching functors are evaluated on lattices in V(λ)⊗σ(τ) (§6.2, PDF127).

api.name: DualWeylModule.mk
api.statement: W(λ)_{/O} := Ind_B^G(w₀λ) for dominant λ, a finite free O-module with G-action.

api.name: DualWeylModule.generic_irreducible
api.statement: W(λ)_{/E} is the irreducible G_{/E}-module of highest weight λ.

api.name: DualWeylModule.socle_special
api.statement: soc W(λ)_{/F} = L(λ), the irreducible G_{/F}-module of highest weight λ.

api.name: DualWeylModule.virtual
api.statement: For arbitrary λ, W(λ) := Σ_i (−1)^i R^iInd_B^G(w₀λ) in the Grothendieck group; for dominant λ it is the class of the genuine module.

api.name: DualWeylModule.dot_reflection
api.statement: W(w·λ) = (−1)^{ℓ(w)} W(λ) for w ∈ W, and W(λ) = 0 if ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ = 0 for some α.

tests.name: DualWeylModule.GL2_sym
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = (a,0) with a ≥ 0, W(λ)_{/E} ≅ Sym^a(E²) has dimension a+1.

tests.name: DualWeylModule.trivial
tests.statement: W(0) is the trivial module.

tests.name: DualWeylModule.GL2_p_reducible
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = (p,0), W(λ)_{/F} = Sym^p(F²) has dimension p+1 but its socle L((p,0)) is the Frobenius twist of the standard module, of dimension 2; so W(λ)_{/F} is not irreducible.

tests.name: DualWeylModule.GL2_singular
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = (−1,0), ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ = 0, so the virtual class W(λ) vanishes.

items.name: Serre weights and restricted highest weights
items.statement: A Serre weight is an irreducible F-representation of G0(Fp). In the paper's finite reductive-group setup, write F(lambda)=L(lambda) restricted to G0(Fp) for lambda in X1={0<=simple-root pairing<=p-1}. Classes are parametrized by X1/(p-pi)X0. Regular means all these pairings are strictly less than p-1; m-depth is that of lambda. Coefficient F is sufficiently large for absolute irreducibility and definition of every weight.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Jantzen's criterion describes Serre-weight constituents of R̄ (Proposition 2.3.6).
Components C_σ^ζ are labelled by Serre weights (Definition 4.6.1).
Emerton–Gee components are Serre-labelled (§7.4).
Modular Serre weights (Definition 9.1.1).

api.name: SerreWeight.mk
api.statement: F(λ) := L(λ)|_{G₀(F_p)} for λ ∈ X₁(T) = {λ : 0 ≤ ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ ≤ p−1 for all simple α}.

api.name: SerreWeight.exists
api.statement: Every irreducible F-representation of G₀(F_p) is isomorphic to some F(λ), and is absolutely irreducible.

api.name: SerreWeight.eq_iff
api.statement: F(λ) ≅ F(λ′) iff λ − λ′ ∈ (p−π)X⁰(T) ([33, Lemma 9.2.4]).

api.name: SerreWeight.IsRegular_def
api.statement: F(λ) is regular iff ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ < p−1 for every simple α; this is independent of the representative λ.

api.name: SerreWeight.IsDeep_def
api.statement: F(λ) is m-deep iff λ is; shifts by (p−π)X⁰(T) preserve depth.

api.name: SerreWeight.le_dualWeyl
api.statement: F(λ) ⊂ W̄(λ) for λ ∈ X₁(T).

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_count
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p (f = 1) there are p(p−1) Serre weights Sym^r⊗det^a, with 0 ≤ r ≤ p−1 and a mod p−1.

tests.name: SerreWeight.trivial
tests.statement: F(0) is the trivial representation.

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_non_injective
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p, F(λ) ≅ F(λ + (p−1)(1,1)); λ ↦ F(λ) is not injective on X₁(T).

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_dim
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p and 0 ≤ r ≤ p−1, F((r,0)) = Sym^r(F²) has dimension r+1.

items.name: Shifted p-alcoves and dot action
items.statement: For z=w t_nu define z dot lambda=w(lambda+eta+p nu)-eta. The shifted p-alcoves are components of the complement of H_(alpha,pn)-eta. C0 has 0<
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Serre weights are presented as F(π⁻¹(w̃₁)·(ω−η)) (2.5).
Jantzen's criterion is phrased with dot-translated p-alcoves (Proposition 2.3.6).
κ = π⁻¹(w̃)·(ω−η) gives a diagonal tame presentation (Proposition 2.4.5).
The linkage principle and dot action bound constituent depth (Lemma 2.2.1).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dotAct_apply
api.statement: (w t_ν)·λ = w(λ + η + pν) − η.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dotAct_mul
api.statement: x·(y·λ) = (xy)·λ and 1·λ = λ; the dot action is the p-scaled affine action conjugated by translation by −η.

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dotAct_transitive
api.statement: W̃ acts transitively on p-alcoves, W_a simply transitively, and Ω = Stab(C₀).

api.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dominant_iff_dot
api.statement: W̃⁺ = {w̃ : w̃·C₀ dominant} and W̃₁⁺ = {w̃ ∈ W̃⁺ : w̃·C₀ p-restricted}, the same sets as in N02.

api.name: Weight.IsDeep.dotAct'
api.statement: λ and w̃·λ have the same depth.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dotAct_fixed
tests.statement: For GL₂, the reflection s fixes −η under the dot action: s·(−η) = −η.

tests.name: ExtAffineWeyl.dotAct_central
tests.statement: For ν ∈ X⁰(T), t_ν·λ = λ + pν.

items.name: Constituent depth bound
items.statement: If dominant mu is not m-deep, h is an integer bounding <mu,alpha^vee> for every root, and sigma is a Jordan–Hölder factor of W(mu), then sigma is not (m+floor(h/(p-1)))-deep. Proof uses linkage, Steinberg tensor product, tensor-weight translation, convexity and a terminating height reduction; none may be replaced by an assumed constituent classification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Dominant translate remains in a Weyl polytope
items.statement: If lambda is dominant, nu is in Conv(W kappa), and w(lambda+nu) is dominant, then w(lambda+nu)-lambda lies in Conv(W kappa). The proof moves across root walls and keeps each corrected nu on a segment between two Weyl conjugates.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Algebraic and finite central characters
items.statement: Algebraic central characters are X*(Z), finite central characters X*(Z)/(p-pi)X*(Z), identified with Hom(Z0(Fp),F^times). F(lambda) has central character lambda restricted to Z modulo (p-pi). Identify X*(Z) with Wtilde/Wa where the source uses this identification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The central lift of a presentation reduces to the central character (Lemma 2.2.3).
0-deep presentations are classified by central lifts (Lemma 2.2.4, with E2).
Deligne–Lusztig presentations are classified by central lifts (Lemma 2.3.2).
The E/F shift ζ ↦ ζ − η|_Z of Remark 2.4.2 (Lemma 2.4.4).

api.name: CentralChar.reduce
api.statement: X*(Z) → X*(Z)/(p−π)X*(Z), sending an algebraic central character to a central character.

api.name: CentralChar.equiv_hom
api.statement: X*(Z)/(p−π)X*(Z) ≅ Hom(Z₀(F_p), F^×).

api.name: CentralChar.ofSerreWeight
api.statement: The central character of F(λ) is λ|_Z mod (p−π)X*(Z), independent of λ ∈ λ + (p−π)X⁰(T).

api.name: CentralChar.equiv_quotient
api.statement: X*(Z) ≅ W̃/W_a, sending the class of t_νw to ν|_Z.

tests.name: CentralChar.GL2_f1
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p, X*(Z) = Z via λ ↦ λ₁+λ₂; Sym^r⊗det^a has central character r+2a mod p−1.

tests.name: CentralChar.torus
tests.statement: If G = T, then Z = T and X*(Z) = X*(T).

tests.name: CentralChar.lift_not_unique
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p, λ and λ + (p−1)(1,1) give the same Serre weight but algebraic central characters differing by 2(p−1).

tests.name: CentralChar.f2_index
tests.statement: For GL₁ with f = 2, p−π acts on X*(Z) = Z² by (a,b) ↦ (pa−b, pb−a), with index p²−1 = |F_{p²}^×|.

items.name: Lowest-alcove presentation of a Serre weight
items.statement: For omega-eta in C0 and w1 in W1plus put F_(w1,omega)=F(pi^-1(w1) dot (omega-eta)). Quotient pairs by (w1,omega)~(t_nu w1,omega-nu) for nu in X0. A presentation is this equivalence class, not a unique unquotiented pair.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Constituents of R̄⊗W(λ) are the F_{(w̃₁, w̃(R)w̃₂⁻¹(0))} (2.8).
Herzig weights are F_{(w̃, w̃(τ̄)w̃₂⁻¹(0))} (2.14).
Covering is tested on compatible presentations (Proposition 2.3.12).
Definition 4.6.1 labels components by a presentation and a central lift.

api.name: SerreWeight.ofPresentation
api.statement: F_{(w̃₁,ω)} := F(π⁻¹(w̃₁)·(ω−η)) for w̃₁ ∈ W̃₁⁺ and ω−η ∈ C₀ ∩ X*(T).

api.name: SerreWeight.ofPresentation_equiv
api.statement: (w̃₁, ω) ~ (t_νw̃₁, ω−ν) for ν ∈ X⁰(T), and equivalent pairs give the same weight.

api.name: SerreWeight.presentations_orbit
api.statement: If (w̃₁, ω) presents σ, its presentations are {(w̃₁π(δ⁻¹), δ·(ω−η)+η) : δ ∈ Ω} up to ~ (proof of Lemma 2.2.4).

api.name: SerreWeight.ofPresentation_deep_iff
api.statement: F_{(w̃₁,ω)} is m-deep iff m < ⟨ω, α^∨⟩ < p−m for all α ∈ Φ⁺.

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_presentation
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p and 0 ≤ r ≤ p−2, (1, (r+1,0)) presents F((r,0)) = Sym^r.

tests.name: SerreWeight.presentation_X0
tests.statement: For ν ∈ X⁰(T), (w̃₁, ω) and (t_νw̃₁, ω−ν) present the same weight.

tests.name: SerreWeight.presentation_frobenius
tests.statement: For f = 2, the j-th component of π⁻¹(w̃₁)·(ω−η) uses the (j−1)-th component of w̃₁; in particular component 0 uses w̃_{1,1}.

tests.name: SerreWeight.presentation_needs_C0
tests.statement: (w̃₁, ω) with ω−η ∉ C₀, for example ω−η on a p-wall, is not a lowest-alcove presentation.

items.name: Compatibility of Serre-weight presentations
items.statement: The algebraic central lift of (w1,omega) is the image of t_(omega-eta) w1 in Wtilde/Wa=X*(Z). Compatible presentations have the same such lift; this is independent of the chosen representative pair.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The central lift reduces to the central character (Lemma 2.2.3).
Constituents of R̄⊗W(λ) have λ-compatible presentations (Proposition 2.3.7).
Herzig weights have presentations compatible with that of τ̄ (Proposition 2.6.2).
C_σ^ζ depends on the central lift ζ (Definition 4.6.1).

api.name: SerreWeight.centralLift
api.statement: ζ(w̃₁, ω) := the class of t_{ω−η}w̃₁ in W̃/W_a ≅ X*(Z) (2.6)–(2.7).

api.name: SerreWeight.centralLift_equiv
api.statement: ζ is constant on ~-classes: t_{ω−ν−η}t_νw̃₁ = t_{ω−η}w̃₁.

api.name: SerreWeight.centralLift_reduce
api.statement: ζ(w̃₁, ω) mod (p−π)X*(Z) is the central character of F_{(w̃₁,ω)} (Lemma 2.2.3).

api.name: SerreWeight.Compatible_def
api.statement: Two presentations are compatible iff they have the same ζ.

api.name: SerreWeight.centralLift_bijective
api.statement: For 0-deep σ, the presentations of σ correspond bijectively to the algebraic central characters lifting its central character; the E2 correction uses t_{ω−η}w̃₁.

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_centralLift
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p, the presentation (1, (r+1,0)) has ζ = r ∈ Z = X*(Z), lifting the central character r mod p−1 of Sym^r.

tests.name: SerreWeight.centralLift_eta_shift
tests.statement: The printed Lemma 2.2.4 formula w̃₁t_ω changes ζ by η|_Z (by 1 for GL₂) and no longer lifts the central character; see E2.

tests.name: SerreWeight.centralLift_X0
tests.statement: Equivalent pairs (w̃₁, ω) and (t_νw̃₁, ω−ν) have the same ζ.

items.name: Central character of a lowest-alcove presentation
items.statement: The lift in(2.7) reduces modulo(p-pi) to the central character of F_(w1,omega).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Presentations classified by central lifts
items.statement: For a0-deep Serre weight sigma, (w1,omega) maps to the class of t_(omega-eta)w1 and bijects its lowest-alcove presentations with algebraic lifts of its finite central character. The printed formula omits -eta; retaining it would change the target character.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig representations
items.statement: For a good pair(s,mu) in W times X*(T), attach the E-representation R_s(mu) of G0(Fp), using the Deligne–Lusztig construction and the sign convention of the cited inputs. A lowest-alcove presentation is(s,mu-eta) with mu-eta in C0; good-pair construction is an external prerequisite, not a formal symbol.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Jantzen's criterion computes JH(R̄) (Proposition 2.3.6).
σ(τ) for tame WD types are the constituents of R_s(μ) (Proposition 2.5.5).
Every R_s(μ) has a bounded presentation (Lemma 2.3.3).
Non-generic Deligne–Lusztig representations are excluded in §8.4 (PDF172).

api.name: DLRep.mk
api.statement: For a good pair (s, μ) ∈ W × X*(T), R_s(μ) is the E-representation of G₀(F_p) attached by [33, Propositions 9.2.1–9.2.2].

api.name: DLRep.shift
api.statement: R_s(μ) ≅ R_s(μ + pν − sπ(ν)) for ν ∈ X*(T) (proof of Lemma 2.3.3).

api.name: DLRep.conj
api.statement: R_s(μ) ≅ R_{wsπ(w)⁻¹}(w(μ)) for w ∈ W.

api.name: DLRep.good_of_deep
api.statement: (s, μ) is good if μ−η is 0-deep in C₀ ([56, Lemma 2.2.3]).

api.name: DLRep.irreducible_of_generic
api.statement: A 1-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation is irreducible ([19, Theorem 6.8]).

api.name: DLRep.ofTameParam
api.statement: V_φ(τ(w, μ)) = R_w(μ) ([33, Proposition 9.2.1], PDF48).

tests.name: DLRep.GL2_principal
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p and s = 1, R_1(μ) has dimension p+1 (a principal series), irreducible when μ₁ ≢ μ₂ mod p−1.

tests.name: DLRep.GL2_cuspidal
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p and s the transposition, R_s(μ) has virtual dimension p−1 and is an irreducible cuspidal representation (from the nonsplit torus) when (s, μ) is 1-generic.

tests.name: DLRep.torus
tests.statement: For G = T a torus, R_1(μ) is the Teichmüller lift of the character μ of T(F_p).

tests.name: DLRep.not_injective
tests.statement: (s, μ) ↦ R_s(μ) is not injective: μ and μ + pν − sπ(ν) give isomorphic representations.

items.name: Generic Deligne–Lusztig presentation
items.statement: R is m-generic if it has a lowest-alcove presentation(s,mu-eta) of depth m. After choosing it, wtilde(R)=t_mu s and w(R)=s; an unchosen representation has no distinguished such element.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Proposition 2.3.7 needs an m-generic presentation, m ≥ max{2h_η, h_{λ+η}}.
The intervals criterion is stated for a max{2h_η, h_{λ+η}}-generic presentation (Proposition 2.3.8).
The covering proof enumerates 2h_η-generic R (PDF44).

api.name: DLRep.IsGeneric_def
api.statement: R is m-generic iff it has a lowest-alcove presentation (s, μ−η) ∈ W × C₀ with μ−η m-deep.

api.name: DLRep.affineElt
api.statement: For a chosen presentation, w̃(R) = t_μ s ∈ W̃ and w(R) = s ∈ W.

api.name: DLRep.isGeneric_iff_affine
api.statement: A presentation is m-generic iff w̃(R) is m-generic (Definition 2.1.10(2)).

api.name: DLRep.IsGeneric.mono
api.statement: If m′ ≤ m, m-generic implies m′-generic.

tests.name: DLRep.GL2_generic
tests.statement: For GL₂, p = 7, s = 1 and μ = (4,0), μ−η = (3,0) ∈ C₀ and R_1(μ) is 2-generic but this presentation is not 3-generic.

tests.name: DLRep.zeroGeneric_iff
tests.statement: R is 0-generic iff it has a lowest-alcove presentation.

tests.name: DLRep.affineElt_depends
tests.statement: w̃(R) depends on the chosen presentation: another presentation (wsπ(w)⁻¹, w(μ+pν−sπ(ν))−η) gives a different element of W̃.

items.name: Generic Deligne–Lusztig irreducibility
items.statement: A1-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation is irreducible; a0-deep lowest-alcove pair is good. Inputs are[19] Theorem6.8 and[56] Lemma2.2.3.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Central compatibility of Deligne–Lusztig presentations
items.statement: A presentation(s,mu-eta) is lambda-compatible with zeta if t_lambda t_mu s has class zeta in Wtilde/Wa. Compatibility with a Serre presentation uses its lift from(2.7). The finite central character of R tensor W(lambda) is zeta modulo(p-pi).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Constituents of R̄⊗W(λ) have λ-compatible presentations (Proposition 2.3.7).
Proposition 2.3.8 assumes λ-compatible presentations of σ and R.
Proposition 2.6.4 compares λ-compatible presentations of ρ̄ and τ.
§8.6 uses λ-compatible presentations (PDF174–178).

api.name: DLPres.LambdaCompatible_def
api.statement: (s, μ−η) is λ-compatible with ζ ∈ X*(Z) iff the class of t_λt_μs in W̃/W_a is ζ; 0-compatible is called compatible.

api.name: DLPres.compatible_centralChar
api.statement: If (s, μ−η) is λ-compatible with ζ, then ζ mod (p−π)X*(Z) is the central character of R⊗W(λ); for λ = 0, of R.

api.name: DLPres.compatible_serre
api.statement: (s, μ−η) and a Serre presentation (w̃₁, ω) are λ-compatible iff the first is λ-compatible, and the second compatible, with one ζ.

api.name: DLPres.lambdaCompatible_shift
api.statement: (s, μ−η) is λ-compatible with ζ iff it is compatible with ζ − λ|_Z.

tests.name: DLPres.GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂, s = 1 and μ = (a,b), the presentation (1, μ−η) is compatible with ζ = a+b.

tests.name: DLPres.zero
tests.statement: 0-compatibility is compatibility.

tests.name: DLPres.not_eta_shift
tests.statement: The class used is that of t_μs, not t_{μ−η}s: for GL₂ and s = 1 these differ by η|_Z = 1.

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig presentations and central lifts
items.statement: For1-generic R, (s,mu-eta) maps to t_mu s modulo Wa and bijects its lowest-alcove presentations with algebraic lifts of its reduced finite central character.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: A bounded presentation for every Deligne–Lusztig representation
items.statement: Every R has R=R_s(mu) with mu dominant and h_mu<=p+2; consequently mu-eta is(-3)-deep in C0. For products of GLn the stronger(-1)-depth is available as Remark2.3.5 records, but needs its own justification.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Deep constituents force generic types
items.statement: For dominant lambda with h_(lambda+eta)<p-3, if JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) contains an m-deep weight, then R admits(s,mu) with mu-eta(m-h_(lambda+2eta))-deep in C0. In the GLn-product refinement one may replace p-3 by p-1.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Jantzen constituent criterion
items.statement: For a2h_eta-generic presentation(s,mu-eta) of R and lambda in X1, F(lambda) belongs to JH(Rbar) iff some z=w t_nu in Wplus satisfies z dot(mu-s pi(nu)-eta) upward wh dot lambda and z dot C0 upward wh dot C0.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible-pair parametrization of tensor constituents
items.statement: For dominant lambda, m>=max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta)), and a chosen m-generic presentation of R, (w1,w2) maps to F_(w1,wtilde(R)w2^-1(0)) and bijects AP(lambda+eta) with JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)). These are sets of constituents; this does not assert multiplicity one.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Depth and central compatibility of tensor constituents
items.statement: With the hypotheses of N40, every constituent is(m-h_(lambda+eta))-deep, and its displayed lowest-alcove presentation is lambda-compatible with that of R.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Constituents by translated Bruhat intervals
items.statement: For dominant lambda, lambda-compatible lowest-alcove presentations(w1,omega) of sigma and(s,mu-eta) of R, and R max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic, sigma lies in JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) iff t_omega W_le_(w0 w1) is contained in t_mu s Adm(lambda+eta).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Outer constituents
items.statement: For R max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic, JHout(Rbar tensor W(lambda)) is the subset under N40 corresponding to pairs(w1,wh t_-lambda w1).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Outer constituents control upper-arrow inequalities (Lemma 2.3.9).
The covering proof uses R with F_{(w̃,ω)} ∈ JH_out(R̄) (PDF44).

api.name: JHout_def
api.statement: For R with a max{2h_η, h_{λ+η}}-generic presentation, JH_out(R̄⊗W(λ)) is the image under (2.8) of the pairs (w̃₁, w̃_ht_{−λ}w̃₁) in AP(λ+η).

api.name: JHout_subset
api.statement: JH_out(R̄⊗W(λ)) ⊆ JH(R̄⊗W(λ)).

api.name: JHout.upArrow
api.statement: If F_{(w̃′,ω′)} ∈ JH_out(R̄) and a compatible (w̃,ω) presents a constituent of R̄, then w̃ ↑ t_{w(R)⁻¹(ω′−ω)}w̃′ (Lemma 2.3.9).

tests.name: JHout.GL2_all
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p and λ = 0, both constituents of a 2-generic R̄ are outer: JH_out(R̄) = JH(R̄), of size 2.

tests.name: JHout.GL2_std_proper
tests.statement: For GL₂ and λ = (1,0), JH(R̄⊗Std) has 4 generic constituents but JH_out has 2.

tests.name: JHout.pair_in_AP
tests.statement: (w̃₁, w̃_ht_{−λ}w̃₁) satisfies the ↑ condition of AP(λ+η) with equality.

items.name: Outer constituent controls upper-arrow inequalities
items.statement: If F_(w',omega') is outer in Rbar and(w,omega) is a compatible presentation of any constituent in Rbar, then w upward t_(barw' barw(R)^-1(omega'-omega)) w'. Here the action on the difference uses the finite Weyl part; representatives may be chosen arbitrarily within the compatible classes.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering relation on Serre weights
items.statement: A3h_eta-deep weight sigma0 covers sigma if every2h_eta-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation whose reduction contains sigma0 also contains sigma. This is an intersection condition over all such R.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Covering is characterized by upper-arrow inequalities (Proposition 2.3.12(2)).
Remark 4.7.4(2) reads covering on torus-fixed points of C_σ (PDF98).
Proposition 2.3.12(3) is used in §8.6 (PDF179).

uses.where: Lemma A.2.1 and its use, published PDF189
uses.how: Some σ′ covering σ has M∞(σ′) ≠ 0, and Proposition 2.3.12(2) then forces σ′ = σ.

api.name: SerreWeight.Covers_def
api.statement: For 3h_η-deep σ₀, σ₀ covers σ iff every 2h_η-generic Deligne–Lusztig R with σ₀ ∈ JH(R̄) also has σ ∈ JH(R̄).

api.name: SerreWeight.Covers.partialOrder
api.statement: Covering is a partial order on 3h_η-deep Serre weights (Remark 2.3.11).

api.name: SerreWeight.covers_iff_upArrow
api.statement: With compatible presentations and ω−η 3h_η-deep, F_{(w̃,ω)} covers F_{(w̃′,ω′)} iff w̃′ ↑ t_{W(ω−ω′)}w̃; then ℓ(w̃′) ≤ ℓ(w̃), with equality iff the presentations are equivalent.

api.name: SerreWeight.covers_iff_interval
api.statement: ⟺ t_{ω′}W̃_{≤w₀w̃′} ⊂ t_ωW̃_{≤w₀w̃} (Proposition 2.3.12(3)).

api.name: SerreWeight.covers_of_linkage
api.statement: If σ ∈ JH(W̄(w̃·(ω−η))), then F_{(w̃,ω)} covers σ (Remark 2.3.13(2)).

tests.name: SerreWeight.covers_refl
tests.statement: Every 3h_η-deep weight covers itself.

tests.name: SerreWeight.GL2_covers_eq
tests.statement: For GL₂, W̃₁⁺ modulo X⁰ is Ω, whose elements have length 0; by the length criterion, covering between 3-deep weights is equality.

tests.name: SerreWeight.covers_of_upArrow
tests.statement: If μ ↑ λ in the dot-linkage order and both weights are in range, F(λ) covers F(μ) (Remark 2.3.13(1)).

tests.name: SerreWeight.covers_not_linkage
tests.statement: The converse fails for GL₄: covering does not imply μ ↑ λ (Remark 2.3.13(1)).

items.name: Covering criterion by alcove inequalities
items.statement: For compatible presentations(w,omega),(w',omega') with omega-eta3h_eta-deep, F_(w,omega) covers F_(w',omega') iff w' upward t_(s(omega-omega')) w for every s in W. Consequently l(w')<=l(w), with equality iff the presentations are equivalent.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering criterion by intervals
items.statement: Under N46's hypotheses, covering is equivalent to t_omega' W_le_(w0 w') being contained in t_omega W_le_(w0 w).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Covering criterion by algebraic modules
items.statement: Under N46's hypotheses, covering is equivalent to F_(w',omega') occurring in the restriction to G0(Fp) of the direct sum of L(pi^-1(w1) dot(omega-eta)) over w1 in Wplus with w1 upward w. On3h_eta-deep weights this gives a partial order, with antisymmetry from the length equality criterion.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame inertial L-parameters from Weyl data
items.statement: For(w,mu), set Fstar=p pi^-1 on the dual cocharacter lattice and choose d with(Fstar w^-1)^d=p^d. Evaluate the cocharacter sum_(i=0)^(d-1)(Fstar w^-1)^i(mu) on the fundamental character omega_d. The conjugacy class tau(w,mu) is independent of d and every tame inertial L-parameter arises thus. Reduction and Teichmuller lift biject the O,E,F versions.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Regularity and genericity of tame types are defined through τ(s, μ) (Definition 2.4.3).
Changing a diagonal presentation (Proposition 2.4.5).
V_φ(τ(w, μ)) = R_w(μ) links tame types to Deligne–Lusztig representations (PDF48, Proposition 2.5.5).
Kisin-module shapes are defined relative to τ(s, μ+η) (§5, PDF99, 122).

api.name: TameParam.ofWeyl
api.statement: τ(w, μ) := (Σ_{i=0}^{d−1}(F*∘w⁻¹)^i(μ))(ω_d) : I_{Q_p} → T^∨(E), with F* = pπ⁻¹ and d ≥ 1 such that (F*∘w⁻¹)^d = p^d.

api.name: TameParam.ofWeyl_indep
api.statement: The G^∨-conjugacy class of τ(w, μ) does not depend on the admissible d.

api.name: TameParam.surjective
api.statement: Every tame inertial L-parameter over E (resp. F) is some τ(w, μ) (resp. τ̄(w, μ)).

api.name: TameParam.reduce_equiv
api.statement: −⊗_O E and −⊗_O F give bijections between tame inertial L-parameters over O, E and F; the inverse of reduction is the Teichmüller lift.

api.name: TameParam.shift
api.statement: τ(w, μ) ≅ τ(w, μ + pν − wπ(ν)) for ν ∈ X*(T), matching DLRep.shift under V_φ.

tests.name: TameParam.GL1
tests.statement: For GL₁ and f = 1, τ(1, a) = ω₁^a.

tests.name: TameParam.GL2_nonsplit
tests.statement: For GL₂, f = 1 and s the transposition, d = 2 and τ(s, (a,b)) = ω₂^{a+pb} ⊕ ω₂^{b+pa}.

tests.name: TameParam.zero
tests.statement: τ(w, 0) is trivial.

tests.name: TameParam.GL2_not_level1
tests.statement: τ(s, (1,0)) = ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^p for GL₂ does not factor through ω₁, since p+1 ∤ 1.

items.name: Explicit tame inertia characters for GLn
items.statement: For unramified K/Qp of degree f and(s,mu+eta), s_tau=s0...s_(f-1), r=ord(s_tau), alpha_j=s_(f-1)^-1...s_(f-j)^-1(mu_(f-j)+eta_(f-j)), a0=sum_(j=0)^(f-1)p^j alpha_j. The type is the direct sum over i of omega_(fr) raised to sum_(k=0)^(r-1)p^(fk) a0_(s_tau^k(i)). It is independent of the algebraic-closure isomorphism used to derive the formula.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: 1-generic GL_n tame inertia has distinct characters χ_i (Example 2.4.1).
The descent datum acts through the characters χ_i⁻¹ of (2.12) (§5.1, PDF102).
Orientations are built from α_j and a^{(0)} (PDF102–103; Remark 5.1.7).
The explicit characters compare tame types with Hodge–Tate data.

api.name: TameType.alpha_def
api.statement: α₀ = μ₀+η₀ and α_j = s_{f−1}⁻¹⋯s_{f−j}⁻¹(μ_{f−j}+η_{f−j}) for 1 ≤ j ≤ f−1; a^{(0)} = Σ_j p^jα_j.

api.name: TameType.chi_def
api.statement: With s_τ = s₀s₁⋯s_{f−1} of order r, χ_i := ω_{fr}^{Σ_{k=0}^{r−1} a^{(0)}_{s_τ^k(i)} p^{fk}}.

api.name: TameType.power_eq
api.statement: (F*∘s⁻¹)^{fr} = p^{fr} on X*(T^∨), which justifies d = fr.

api.name: TameType.indep_iota
api.statement: The characters χ_i depend only on τ(s, μ+η), not on the chosen isomorphism K̄ → Q̄_p.

tests.name: TameType.GL2_split
tests.statement: For f = 1, n = 2, s = 1 and μ = (a,b), χ₁ = ω₁^{a+1} and χ₂ = ω₁^b.

tests.name: TameType.GL2_nonsplit
tests.statement: For f = 1, n = 2 and s the transposition, r = 2, χ₁ = ω₂^{(a+1)+pb} and χ₂ = ω₂^{b+p(a+1)}, agreeing with τ(s, μ+η) from N49.

tests.name: TameType.order_convention
tests.statement: The convention differs from [56, 59] as explained in Remark 5.1.7; the s_τ of Example 2.4.1 coincides with that of [56, §3.2].

items.name: Lowest-alcove presentations and the E/F central shift
items.statement: A presentation(s,mu) has mu in C0 and tau=tau(s,mu+eta). For E-valued tau, lambda-compatibility uses t_lambda t_(mu+eta)s modulo Wa. For F-valued bartau, compatibility uses t_mu s modulo Wa. Reduction therefore changes the compatible central lift by -eta restricted to Z; do not identify the two conventions.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Lemma 2.4.4 classifies presentations over E by ζ with ζ∘ω₁ = det∘τ.
Over F, by ζ with (ζ−η|_Z)∘ω₁ = det∘τ̄ (with the E3 correction).
Proposition 2.6.4 fixes λ-compatible presentations of ρ̄ and τ.
Residual genericity is measured through lowest-alcove presentations (Definition 5.5.1, PDF122).
Theorem 9.1.6 assumes a P-generic lowest-alcove presentation (PDF184).

api.name: TamePres_def
api.statement: (s, μ) with μ ∈ C₀ is a lowest-alcove presentation of τ (resp. τ̄) iff τ ≅ τ(s, μ+η) (resp. τ̄ ≅ τ̄(s, μ+η)).

api.name: TamePres.affineElt
api.statement: For a fixed presentation, w̃(τ) = t_{μ+η}s (resp. w̃(τ̄) = t_{μ+η}s).

api.name: TamePres.LambdaCompatibleE_def
api.statement: Over E, (s, μ) is λ-compatible with ζ iff the class of t_λt_{μ+η}s in W̃/W_a is ζ.

api.name: TamePres.CompatibleF_def
api.statement: Over F, (s, μ) is compatible with ζ iff the class of t_μs is ζ.

api.name: TamePres.reduce_shift
api.statement: If (s, μ) is compatible with ζ for τ, it is compatible with ζ − η|_Z for τ̄ (Remark 2.4.2).

api.name: TamePres.det
api.statement: ζ∘ω₁ = det∘τ over E, and (ζ−η|_Z)∘ω₁ = det∘τ̄ over F.

tests.name: TamePres.GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂, f = 1, s = 1 and μ = (a,b) ∈ C₀: τ = ω₁^{a+1} ⊕ ω₁^b, the E-compatible ζ is a+b+1 = the exponent of det τ, and the F-compatible class is a+b = ζ − η|_Z.

tests.name: TamePres.GL1
tests.statement: For GL₁ (η = 0), the E and F conventions agree.

tests.name: TamePres.no_identify
tests.statement: Using the E convention for τ̄ gives ζ with ζ∘ω₁ ≠ det∘τ̄ whenever η|_Z ≢ 0 mod (p−π)X*(Z), for example for GL₂.

items.name: Regular and generic tame types
items.statement: Regular means each coroot evaluated on a torus-valued conjugate is nontrivial. m-generic means a lowest-alcove presentation(s,mu) with mu m-deep exists. With a chosen presentation set wtilde(tau)=t_(mu+eta)s. These notions apply to F types as well. One-generic implies regular; having a lowest-alcove presentation is equivalent to0-genericity.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Converts a lowest-alcove depth bound into distinct inertia characters.
Transfers depth through a height-bounded lattice.
Supplies the semisimplicity bridge for tame consumers.

api.name: TameType.isRegular_iff_distinct
api.statement: For GL_n, regularity is equivalent to pairwise distinct inertia characters after a finite splitting-field extension.

api.name: TameType.generic_mono
api.statement: If 0≤m′≤m and τ is m-generic, it is m′-generic with the same presentation.

api.name: TameType.oneGeneric_regular
api.statement: A 1-generic GL_n type is regular, with the exponent-separation proof K45.

api.name: TameType.regular_baseChange
api.statement: Regularity and an explicitly given generic lowest-alcove presentation persist and reflect under injective coefficient extension.

api.name: TameType.presentation_affineElement
api.statement: A chosen (s,μ) gives w(τ)=t_(μ+η)s; changing a presentation requires the specified affine equivalence, not literal equality.

tests.name: TameType.rankOne
tests.statement: For GL_1, no roots occur; regularity is vacuous and there is a single inertia character.

tests.name: TameType.boundaryCollision
tests.statement: For GL_2, f=1, s=1 and μ+η=(p−1,0), the presentation is 0-generic but the two level-one fundamental-character powers coincide. One-genericity fails.

tests.name: TameType.centralShift
tests.statement: Adding the same integer to every coordinate in one embedding changes the common character twist but preserves all exponent differences and regularity.

tests.name: TameType.positiveGap
tests.statement: For p=7, f=1, s=1 and μ+η=(4,2,0), the inertia exponents 4,2,0 are distinct modulo6 and all positive-root differences lie strictly between1 and6.

items.name: Characteristic-zero types and determinant lifts
items.statement: For1-generic tau over E, (s,mu) maps to t_(mu+eta)s modulo Wa and bijects lowest-alcove presentations with zeta in X*(Z) satisfying zeta composed with omega1=det tau.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual types and determinant lifts
items.locator: Lemma2.4.4, second part, PDF48, corrected E3
items.statement: For1-generic bartau, the map(s,mu)->t_mu s modulo Wa bijects lowest-alcove presentations with zeta such that(zeta+eta restricted to Z) composed with baromega1=det bartau. The printed minus sign contradicts the definition of tau(s,mu+eta).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Changing a diagonal tame presentation
items.statement: For z=t_nu w, omega a weight and kappa=pi^-1(z) dot(omega-eta), tau(1,kappa) is isomorphic to tau(pi^-1(w)^-1 w, omega+pi^-1(w)^-1(nu-eta)).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Weil–Deligne inertial parameter
items.statement: A pair(rho_tau,N_tau) consists of an open-kernel inertia homomorphism and a nilpotent Lie element, admitting a Weil extension with Ad(rho(g))N_tau=norm(g)N_tau; take conjugacy classes, and for L-parameters require the prescribed projection to the Galois factor. For a local field K use its Weil group and its residue cardinality in the norm. Tameness concerns rho_tau, and an ordinary inertial type is the N_tau=0 subcase.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 2.5.4 attaches σ(τ) to WD inertial types.
Deformation rings R_ρ^{λ,τ} for WD inertial types (§6.1, PDF126).
Types (λ+η, τ) with τ a WD inertial type (§8.1, PDF163).
Theorem A.4.1 fixes WD inertial types τ_v (PDF196).

api.name: WDInertialType.mk
api.statement: A WD inertial L-homomorphism is (ρ_τ, N_τ), with ρ_τ : I_{Q_p} → G^∨(E) of open kernel and N_τ ∈ Lie G^∨(E) nilpotent, admitting an L-homomorphism ρ extending ρ_τ with ρ(g)N_τρ(g)⁻¹ = ‖g‖N_τ; types are G^∨(E)-conjugacy classes.

api.name: WDInertialType.ofInertial
api.statement: An inertial type τ gives the WD inertial type (τ, 0); forgetting N is a left inverse.

api.name: WDInertialType.IsTame_def
api.statement: (ρ_τ, N_τ) is tame iff ρ_τ factors through tame inertia.

api.name: WDInertialType.restrict
api.statement: A WD representation (ρ, N) of W_K restricts to the WD inertial type (ρ|_{I_K}, N).

api.name: WDInertialType.equiv_collection
api.statement: WD inertial L-parameters correspond to collections (τ_v)_{v∈S_p} of WD inertial types, preserving tameness.

tests.name: WDInertialType.zero_N
tests.statement: N = 0 recovers ordinary inertial types, and forgetting N after the inclusion is the identity.

tests.name: WDInertialType.steinberg
tests.statement: For GL₂, (1, [[0,1],[0,0]]) is a WD inertial type: the restriction of the Steinberg WD representation.

tests.name: WDInertialType.N_isotypic
tests.statement: Since ‖g‖ = 1 on inertia, N_τ commutes with ρ_τ(I); if ρ_τ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂, then N_τ = 0.

tests.name: WDInertialType.forget_not_injective
tests.statement: Forgetting N is not injective: (1, 0) and (1, [[0,1],[0,0]]) have the same image.

items.name: Monodromy dominance on inertial types
items.statement: For GLn compare nilpotent conjugacy classes by dominance of their Jordan partitions. Put tau<=tau' when their inertia representations agree and the nilpotent restrictions to every irreducible inertia-isotypic summand compare in this order; for collections compare componentwise. Zero monodromy is minimal.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 2.5.4(1) bounds rec_K(π)|_{I_K} ⪯ τ.
Theorem 2.5.4(3) uses maximality for ⪯.
R_ρ^{λ,⪯τ} is the union over τ′ ⪯ τ (Definition 2.5.3 used on PDF126).
Extremal types are maximal or minimal for ⪯ (PDF163).
The corrected Theorem A.4.1 uses the quotient with monodromy ⪯ τ (E34).

api.name: Partition.DominanceLE_def
api.statement: P₁ ⪯ P₂ iff Σ_{i≤k}P₁(i) ≤ Σ_{i≤k}P₂(i) for all k.

api.name: Nilpotent.DominanceLE_def
api.statement: For nilpotent N₁, N₂ ∈ M_n(E), N₁ ⪯ N₂ iff their Jordan partitions satisfy P_{N₁} ⪯ P_{N₂}.

api.name: WDInertialType.LE_def
api.statement: τ ⪯ τ′ iff ρ_τ ≅ ρ_τ′ and N_τ(τ₀) ⪯ N_τ′(τ₀) for every irreducible inertial type τ₀; for L-parameters, componentwise over v ∈ S_p.

api.name: WDInertialType.le_partialOrder
api.statement: ⪯ is a partial order on WD inertial types.

api.name: WDInertialType.zero_le
api.statement: (ρ_τ, 0) ⪯ (ρ_τ, N) for every N.

tests.name: WDInertialType.GL3_chain
tests.statement: For GL₃ with trivial ρ_τ, the Jordan types (1,1,1) ⪯ (2,1) ⪯ (3).

tests.name: WDInertialType.GL1
tests.statement: For GL₁, N = 0 always and ⪯ is equality.

tests.name: WDInertialType.different_rho
tests.statement: Types with non-isomorphic ρ_τ are incomparable, even when both have N = 0.

tests.name: WDInertialType.orbit_closure
tests.statement: For GL_n, N₁ ⪯ N₂ iff the orbit of N₁ lies in the closure of the orbit of N₂ (Gerstenhaber–Hesselink).

items.name: Occurrence of an inertial type bounds monodromy
items.statement: For any WD inertial type tau of GLn(K) there exists smooth irreducible sigma(tau) of GLn(OK) over sufficiently large E such that its occurrence in an irreducible admissible pi implies rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia <=tau. No uniqueness of sigma(tau) is asserted.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Exact inertial type has multiplicity one
items.statement: For the sigma(tau) supplied in N58, rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia=tau implies multiplicity one of sigma(tau) in pi restricted to GLn(OK).
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic representations and dominated monodromy
items.statement: For the same sigma(tau), if pi is generic and rec_K(pi) restricted to inertia<=tau, then sigma(tau) occurs; its multiplicity is one if additionally tau is maximal in the monodromy order.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame types are constituents of Deligne–Lusztig representations
items.statement: For G=GLn and(s,mu), one can choose the sigma(tau) of N58 as tau=(tau(s,mu),N_tau) varies so that their set is exactly the irreducible constituents of R_s(mu), inflated to GLn(Op). The proof uses cuspidal types, Bernstein covers and parabolic induction; it does not assert an arbitrary previously chosen sigma has this property.
items.note: Route owner: SmoothRepresentationsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Herzig involution and predicted weights
items.statement: For regular sigma=F(lambda), define R(sigma)=F(wh dot lambda); this is well defined and bijective, with square a character twist. For tame bartau put W?(bartau)=R(JH(sigma([bartau]))), with the regular-weight domain understood as in Herzig's recipe and the generic range used subsequently; [bartau] denotes Teichmuller lift.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: W?(τ̄) is parametrized by pairs (w̃, w̃₂) with w̃₂ ↑ w̃ (Proposition 2.6.2).
Weights in W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ(τ)) (Proposition 2.6.4, with E4).
Component membership matches predicted weights (Proposition 7.4.7, PDF162).
Theorem 9.1.6 identifies modular weights with W?(r_p|_{I_{Q_p}}) (PDF183–185).

api.name: SerreWeight.herzigR
api.statement: For regular σ = F(λ), R(σ) := F(w̃_h·λ), with w̃_h = w₀t_{−η}; this is independent of the representative λ.

api.name: SerreWeight.herzigR_bijective
api.statement: R is a bijection of the set of regular Serre weights, and R² is a twist by a character.

api.name: HerzigSet_def
api.statement: For a tame inertial L-parameter τ̄ over F, W?(τ̄) := R(JH(σ̄([τ̄]))), where [τ̄] is the Teichmüller lift.

api.name: HerzigSet.param
api.statement: For an m-generic presentation, m ≥ 2h_η, W?(τ̄) ≃ {(w̃, w̃₂) ∈ W̃₁⁺ × W̃⁺ : w̃₂ ↑ w̃}/X⁰(T) via (w̃, w̃₂) ↦ F_{(w̃, w̃(τ̄)w̃₂⁻¹(0))} (Proposition 2.6.2).

api.name: HerzigSet.deep
api.statement: Elements of W?(τ̄) are (m−h_η)-deep, and their presentations are compatible with that of τ̄.

tests.name: SerreWeight.herzigR_GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂ over F_p with η = (1,0): R(Sym^r⊗det^b) = Sym^{p−2−r}⊗det^{r+b+1−p} for 0 ≤ r ≤ p−2, and R² is the twist by det^{−p}.

tests.name: HerzigSet.GL2_size
tests.statement: For GL₂ and a 2-generic τ̄, W?(τ̄) has 2 elements.

tests.name: HerzigSet.GL3_size
tests.statement: For GL₃ and a 4-generic τ̄, W?(τ̄) has 9 elements: 3 pairs over the lower restricted alcove and 6 over the upper.

tests.name: SerreWeight.herzigR_regular_only
tests.statement: R is defined only on regular weights: for GL₂, F((p−1,0)) is not regular, since ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ = p−1.

items.name: Parametrization of Herzig weights
items.statement: For m>=2h_eta and a chosen m-generic presentation of bartau, pairs(w,w2) in W1plus times Wplus modulo diagonal X0 with w2 upward w map bijectively to W?(bartau) by F_(w,wtilde(bartau)w2^-1(0)).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Depth and compatibility of Herzig weights
items.statement: With N63's hypotheses all the displayed weights are(m-h_eta)-deep and their presentations are compatible with the F-valued presentation of bartau.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious Serre weights
items.statement: Wobv(bartau) is the subset in N63 given by pairs(w,w). Such a weight is determined by the finite Weyl image of w, retaining the presentation convention.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The extremal intersection is a single obvious weight (Corollary 2.6.5).
Admissibility produces an obvious common weight (Proposition 2.6.6).
Detectable patching functors are nonzero on W_obv(ρ̄) (Definition 6.2.1(III)).
σ ∈ W_obv(ρ̄) implies ρ̄ ∈ C_σ (Proposition 7.4.7(1), PDF162).

api.name: HerzigSet.Obv_def
api.statement: W_obv(τ̄) is the image under (2.14) of the pairs (w̃, w̃).

api.name: HerzigSet.obv_subset
api.statement: W_obv(τ̄) ⊆ W?(τ̄).

api.name: HerzigSet.obv_equiv
api.statement: For a fixed 2h_η-generic presentation, W_obv(τ̄) ≃ W via the image w ∈ W of w̃.

api.name: HerzigSet.obv_of_adm
api.statement: If w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η), then W_obv(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)⊗W̄(λ)) ≠ ∅ (Proposition 2.6.6).

api.name: HerzigSet.obv_unique
api.statement: If w̃(ρ̄,τ) = t_{s⁻¹(λ+η)}, then W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)⊗W̄(λ)) is the obvious weight for s (Corollary 2.6.5).

tests.name: HerzigSet.GL2_obv_all
tests.statement: For GL₂ and 2-generic τ̄, W_obv(τ̄) = W?(τ̄), of size 2 = |W|.

tests.name: HerzigSet.GL3_obv_proper
tests.statement: For GL₃ and generic τ̄, W_obv(τ̄) has 6 elements and W?(τ̄) has 9, so the inclusion is proper.

tests.name: HerzigSet.obv_labels
tests.statement: An obvious weight is determined by the image w ∈ W of w̃.

items.name: Relative position of residual and lifted types
items.statement: For lambda-compatible chosen presentations of rhobar over F and tau over E, define wtilde(rhobar,tau)=wtilde(tau)^-1 wtilde(rhobar). It is presentation-dependent data with the specified compatibility, not an invariant without choices.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Proposition 2.6.4 describes W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ(τ)) through w̃(ρ̄,τ).
Corollary 2.6.5 assumes w̃(ρ̄,τ) = t_{s⁻¹(λ+η)}.
Proposition 2.6.6 assumes w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η).
Corollary 5.5.8 proves w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η) when the deformation ring is nonzero (PDF123, 130).

api.name: TamePres.relPos_def
api.statement: For λ-compatible chosen presentations of ρ̄ over F and τ over E, w̃(ρ̄,τ) := w̃(τ)⁻¹w̃(ρ̄).

api.name: TamePres.relPos_class
api.statement: w̃(ρ̄,τ) lies in the W_a-coset with class (λ+η)|_Z in W̃/W_a ≅ X*(Z), the coset of t_{λ+η}; so membership in Adm(λ+η) is a condition within one coset.

api.name: TamePres.relPos_factor
api.statement: A weight with presentation (w̃, ω) lies in W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ(τ)) iff w̃(ρ̄,τ) = w̃₂⁻¹ww̃₁ with w̃₁ ↑ w̃ ↑ t_λw̃_h⁻¹w̃₂ (Proposition 2.6.4, E4).

api.name: TamePres.relPos_presentation
api.statement: w̃(ρ̄,τ) depends on the chosen pair of compatible presentations; it is data, not an invariant of (ρ̄, τ).

tests.name: TamePres.relPos_GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂, f = 1 and λ = 0, presentations (1, μ̄) of ρ̄ and (1, μ) of τ with μ̄ − μ = (1,0) are compatible, and w̃(ρ̄,τ) = t_{(1,0)} = t_η ∈ Adm(η).

tests.name: TamePres.relPos_never_one
tests.statement: For GL_n with n ≥ 2 and λ = 0, w̃(ρ̄,τ) ≠ 1, since its class η|_Z = n(n−1)/2 per embedding is nonzero.

tests.name: TamePres.relPos_class_test
tests.statement: The class of w̃(ρ̄,τ) in W̃/W_a equals (λ+η)|_Z.

items.name: Breuil–Mézard weight-intersection criterion
items.statement: For dominant lambda and lambda-compatible2h_eta-generic rhobar and max(2h_eta,h_(lambda+eta))-generic tau presentations, a compatible(w,omega) represents a weight in W?(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) iff there are w1,w2 in Wplus with w1 upward w upward t_lambda wh^-1 w2 and omega=wtilde(rhobar)w1^-1(0)=wtilde(tau)w2^-1(0). The tensor factor is omitted in the printed first assertion.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine factorization of equal weight parameters
items.statement: In N67's setup, equality of the two expressions for omega holds iff wtilde(rhobar,tau)=w2^-1 s w1 for some finite Weyl s.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extremal intersection is a single obvious weight
items.statement: Under N67's hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau)=t_(s^-1(lambda+eta)) for finite Weyl s, then W?(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) consists of exactly the obvious weight corresponding to s. In the proof the forced equality is w=w1, not the printed w=w2 (E5).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility produces an obvious common weight
items.statement: Under N67's genericity and compatibility hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau) belongs to Adm(lambda+eta), then Wobv(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) is nonempty.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Herzig weights lie in one auxiliary tensor type
items.statement: For a3h_eta-generic chosen bartau presentation, take the eta-compatible Deligne–Lusztig representation R with wtilde(R)=wtilde(bartau)t_(-eta-w0 eta). Then W?(bartau) is contained in JH(Rbar tensor W(eta)); -eta-w0 eta is central.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal Iwahori group scheme
items.statement: Over X=Spec Z[v], construct the smooth affine Bruhat–Tits group scheme G with connected fibres from cyclic n-tuples of invertible matrices satisfying D_i A_(i-1)=A_i D_i, where D_i has v in its ith diagonal position. If v maps to a regular element t in R, its R-points are the invertible matrices upper triangular modulo t. Use the tuple functor for arbitrary bases.
