items.name: Galois norm of an idempotent in a pointed connected algebra
items.statement: Let A be a connected commutative K-algebra with a K-algebra retraction ε:A→K and L/K a finite Galois extension. Every idempotent of L⊗_K A is 0 or 1; thus its spectrum is connected. No normality, reducedness or finite-type hypothesis on A is required.
items.locator: Stacks 33.7.12–14 (0361,04KV), affine finite-Galois specialization; explicit multiplicative-idempotent proof in this report
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0.
proofSteps: Let G act on L⊗A through L. Apply L50 to f(a)=1⊗a; its scalar-extension map is the identity under the tensor identification, so invariants are exactly 1⊗A. This uses trace-one descent, never division by |G|.
For an idempotent e, ε_L(e) is 0 or 1 in L. Replace e by 1−e if necessary to make ε_L(e)=1. Set N(e)=∏_{σ∈G}σ(e). It is invariant, idempotent and evaluates to 1, so N(e)=1 by connectedness of A.
The identity element occurs in the product, and eN(e)=N(e) by e²=e. Thus e=1. Undo the complement. The retraction also proves nontriviality after extension.

items.name: Purely inseparable base change preserves idempotents
items.statement: For any commutative K-algebra A and purely inseparable field extension L/K, the injection A→A⊗_K L induces a bijection on idempotents. In particular connectedness is preserved, including for finite extensions over an imperfect field.
items.locator: Stacks purely inseparable power criterion 09HE; direct finite-support Frobenius argument below
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0.
proofSteps: Write an idempotent e as a finite sum of pure tensors. Choose a common exponent q^n that sends every occurring coefficient of L into K, using L51. The Frobenius map distributes over the finite sum.
Because e^(q^n)=e, e is in the image of A. Faithfulness of scalar extension gives injectivity and reflects idempotence. No inverse-limit or reducedness assumption is involved.

items.name: Finite-extension connectedness of an augmented connected algebra
items.statement: If Spec A is connected for a commutative K-algebra A admitting a K-algebra retraction to K, then Spec(A⊗_K L) is connected for every finite field extension L/K.
items.locator: Stacks 04KV; finite-extension proof assembled from Z45–Z46
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0.
proofSteps: Let E be the separable closure of K in L. Embed the finite separable E/K in a finite Galois closure F/K. Z45 applies to F; the injection A⊗E→A⊗F and L53 give connectedness over E.
Apply L52 and Z46 to the purely inseparable L/E. The original retraction base changes throughout. Characteristic zero simply omits this last step.

items.name: Distinguished coordinates for a nonzero restricted series
items.statement: Over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, any finite family of nonzero elements of K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ (n>0) can simultaneously be made X_n-distinguished by an isometric triangular coordinate change X_i↦X_i+X_n^(t^(n−i)), i<n, X_n↦X_n, for sufficiently large integer t. Distinguished means the leading coefficient is a unit of maximal norm and all higher coefficients have strictly smaller norm.
items.locator: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, Münster notes, §1.2 Lemma7, printed11–12/PDF13–14
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
proofSteps: Normalize each Gauss norm to one. Its reduction has finite support. Choose t above all exponents in these supports; their base-t weighted degrees are distinct. The unique largest degree gives a nonzero scalar leading coefficient after substitution.

The inverse substitution subtracts the same powers. Both maps are contractive, hence isometric. Units are exactly the order-zero case. Use the existing upstream restricted-series evaluation API, not a new series carrier.

items.name: Weierstrass division for Tate algebras
items.statement: For g∈K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ distinguished of degree s in X_n and f in the same algebra, there are unique q in that algebra and r∈K⟨X₁,…,X_(n−1)⟩[X_n] with degree r<s such that f=qg+r. The Gauss norms satisfy |f|=max(|q||g|,|r|). K is complete and nontrivially nonarchimedean.
items.locator: Bosch Münster notes §1.2 Theorem8, printed12–13/PDF14–15; existing AdicSpaces Layer0.5(3)
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation.
proofSteps: After norm normalization truncate g at its distinguished degree. Divide polynomials by this unit-leading polynomial. Choose 0<θ<1 at least the norm of the discarded tail, including when that tail is zero.

Approximate each current series by a polynomial to relative accuracy θ, iterate division and sum q_i,r_i; the errors contract by θ. Completeness gives existence and reduction proves the norm identity and uniqueness. The source proof was read; this existing upstream target is imported, not re-planned.

items.name: Affinoid Noether normalization from distinguished division
items.statement: For a proper ideal I of the strict Tate algebra T_n(K), there exists d≤n and a finite injective K-algebra homomorphism T_d(K)→T_n(K)/I. The map need not be the original coordinate inclusion.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
proofSteps: Induct on n. For I=0 use the identity. Otherwise choose 0≠g∈I and apply Z48. Z49 identifies T_n/(g) as finite free over T_(n−1) with basis 1,X_n,…,X_n^(s−1). Properness excludes s=0.
Apply induction to the kernel of T_(n−1)→T_n/I, then compose finite maps. At n=0 properness forces I=0. The dimension equality in Bosch is not needed for the maximal-residue-field consumer.

items.name: Finite maximal residue fields of strict affinoids
items.statement: Every maximal ideal m of a strict K-affinoid algebra A has residue field finite over K. Consequently every nonempty clopen of Spec A contains a closed point that becomes K′-rational after a finite extension K′/K; finitely many chosen points can be rationalized in one finite extension.
items.locator: Bosch Münster notes §1.2 Corollary11 and §1.4 Proposition2, PDF16,24; BLGGT LemmaA.1.1 PDF96
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
proofSteps: Apply Z50 to the field quotient A/m. An integral subring of a field over which that field is integral must itself be a field; T_d is a field only when d=0 (X₁ is a nonzero nonunit if d>0). Thus A/m is finite over K.

A nonempty clopen is the spectrum of a nonzero idempotent factor, which has a maximal ideal. Embed finitely many finite residue fields in one algebraic closure and take their finite compositum, allowing inseparability. Tensor each residue map with this field and multiply to obtain rational points.

items.name: Strict affinoid completed tensor and quotient presentation
items.statement: For strict K-affinoids A=K⟨X⟩/I and B=K⟨Y⟩/J over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field, their completed tensor is K⟨X,Y⟩/(I,J), with its quotient Banach topology. It represents pairs of continuous K-algebra maps to a commutative Banach K-algebra. Use the existing AdicSpacesPartII:R0 carrier and prove presentation independence.
items.locator: Conrad AWS Exercise2.2.3(1)–(2), PDF13; Example2.4.5, PDF20
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation.
proofSteps: Combine the variables using restricted-series iteration, quotient by the two extended ideals, and use the evaluation universal property. Affinoid ideals are closed, so this is a Banach quotient.

Construct the inverse maps between two presentations by the same universal property and prove they agree on both factors. This supplies a strict affinoid specialization of the owner’s admissible completed tensor, not a second general Huber tensor.

uses.how: Commute finite scalar extension with affinoid products.
Compute fibers over rational points.
Identify the generic fiber of an integral completion.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.factorMaps
api.statement: Provide continuous factor maps A→A⊗̂_K B and B→A⊗̂_K B agreeing on K.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.homEquiv
api.statement: Continuous maps A⊗̂_K B→D correspond to pairs of continuous K-algebra maps A→D,B→D; prove both factor evaluations and uniqueness.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.presentation
api.statement: Identify the tensor with K⟨X,Y⟩/(I,J) respecting coefficients, variables and quotient topologies.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.ext
api.statement: Two continuous maps are equal if they agree on both factors.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.map
api.statement: Pairs of continuous maps induce tensor maps; prove identity, composition and evaluation on pure tensors.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.commAssoc
api.statement: Swap or regroup factors by mutually continuous equivalences; K is the unit.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.quotient
api.statement: For ideals I′⊂A,J′⊂B identify (A/I′)⊗̂(B/J′) with (A⊗̂B)/(I′,J′), using closedness.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.finiteScalar
api.statement: The finite extension specialization and its relation to the ordinary tensor are supplied by Z53.

api.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.rationalFiber
api.statement: For a K-rational point on A, quotienting by its extended kernel gives B as in Z54.

tests.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.unit
tests.statement: K⊗̂_K K=K and K⊗̂_K B=B, with the named factor maps.

tests.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.polydisc
tests.statement: K⟨x⟩⊗̂_K K⟨y⟩=K⟨x,y⟩ and the factor coordinates map to x,y.

tests.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.rationalFiber
tests.statement: For |a|≤1, quotient K⟨x,y⟩ by x−a gives K⟨y⟩; then y−b gives K for |b|≤1.

tests.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.nilpotents
tests.statement: K[ε]/ε²⊗̂_K K[δ]/δ²=K[ε,δ]/(ε²,δ²), so the construction does not assert reducedness.

tests.name: AffinoidCompletedTensor.ordinaryTensor
tests.statement: For K=Q_p, Σ_n p^n x^n y^n belongs to K⟨x,y⟩ but not to K⟨x⟩⊗_K K⟨y⟩: its coefficient matrix has infinite rank whereas a finite sum of separated tensors has finite rank.

items.name: Finite scalar extension of strict affinoids and their products
items.statement: For finite L/K, A⊗_K L is already complete with its finite-module Banach topology and identifies with A⊗̂_K L. If A=K⟨X⟩/I it is L⟨X⟩/I_L, and (A⊗̂_K B)⊗_K L≅(A⊗_K L)⊗̂_L(B⊗_K L), compatibly with all factor maps.
items.locator: Conrad Exercise2.2.3(3), PDF13; BLGGT AppendixA.1 conventions PDF95; finite-basis proof below
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
proofSteps: Choose a K-basis of L. Equivalence of finite-dimensional norms makes a restricted L-coefficient family exactly a tuple of restricted K-coefficient families, hence L⊗T_n(K)≅T_n(L). L54 is the module-level baseline comparison; the multiplicative and topological compatibility remains this adapter.

Flatness over K identifies the quotient kernel with the extended ideal, and closedness of affinoid ideals makes the quotient complete. Apply the two-variable presentation of Z52 on both sides to get the product comparison. No separability or infinite scalar extension is required.

items.name: Fibers of a completed tensor at rational points
items.statement: For strict K-affinoids A,B and a continuous K-algebra retraction ε:A→K with m=ker ε, (A⊗̂_K B)/m(A⊗̂_K B)≅B. For also η:B→K with n=ker η, the quotient by (m,n) is K. The isomorphisms respect both factor maps and Banach quotient topologies.
items.locator: BLGGT LemmaA.1.1 proof PDF96; Conrad Exercise2.2.3, PDF13
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
proofSteps: Use the affinoid quotient presentation to commute quotient with the tensor, then K⊗̂_K B=B. The kernel is the extended ideal itself since it is closed in the Noetherian affinoid, not merely an unspecified dense ideal.

Repeat with B/n. If B is connected, the first fiber is connected and contains the point that supplied ε; this locates that entire fiber in the same clopen part. The second fiber gives the common point used in Z14.

items.name: Finite-type integral models identify generic completed products
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with uniformizer π, K=Frac O, and B_i a finite family of finite-type O-algebras. Set C_i=π-adic completion of B_i and P=⊗_O B_i. Then C=π-adic completion of P identifies with the π-adic completed tensor of the C_i, and C[1/π]≅⊗̂_K(C_i[1/π]). These identifications preserve coefficients and factor maps.
items.locator: Conrad Exercise3.3.1 and 3.3.8, PDF30,32; LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 final paragraph PDF79–80
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:F0.
proofSteps: Write B_i=O[X_i]/I_i with finitely generated I_i. Exactness of completion over O[X_i] gives C_i=O⟨X_i⟩/(I_i). The tensor presentation uses all variables and all relations; the finite-quotient inverse systems also give the canonical integral completed tensor comparison.

A restricted K-series has coefficients bounded below in valuation, hence one common power of π clears them. Therefore O⟨X⟩[1/π]=K⟨X⟩; localization commutes with this quotient. Compare Z52 presentations. This is a bounded-denominator series argument, not a claim that localization commutes with arbitrary inverse limits.

items.name: Flatness of the finite-type integral product completion
items.statement: In Z55, if each B_i is O-flat then C is O-flat, multiplication by π on C is injective, and C→C[1/π] is injective. The empty family gives C=O.
items.locator: LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 final deduction; Mathlib flatness of Noetherian completion and flat tensor/transitivity atoms
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:F0.
proofSteps: The ordinary finite tensor P is O-flat by L55 and finite type over Noetherian O, hence Noetherian. Apply L11 to P and (π): C is P-flat. L56 gives O-flatness, and L57 gives injectivity of π.

Every power of π acts injectively, so the localization kernel is zero. Do not apply Noetherian completion flatness to an arbitrary ordinary tensor of already completed rings: the finite-type P is the presentation ring that justifies it.

items.name: Completion of a G-ring is a regular morphism
items.statement: If P is a Noetherian G-ring and I an ideal, then P→P̂_I is flat with geometrically regular fibers. In particular it remains a regular map after inverting any element. This does not say the completion is a G-ring.
items.locator: Stacks 0AH2 (15.51.14), proof read; 07GG Remark15.51.11 distinguishes G-ringness of the target
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4.
proofSteps: Use flatness and Noetherianity of completion. A maximal ideal of the completion contains I and has the same residue field as its contraction. The resulting local map has the same maximal-ideal completion as P at that contraction.

That local completion map is regular by the G-ring hypothesis. Descend regularity along the faithfully flat map from the localized I-adic completion to the common maximal-ideal completion. The regular-map criterion and this faithful-flat descent are explicit remaining supplier obligations, not baseline results.

items.name: Finite-type algebras over a complete DVR are G-rings
items.statement: If O is a complete DVR and P a finite-type O-algebra, P is a Noetherian G-ring. No perfection assumption on the residue field is made.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4.
proofSteps: O itself is a G-ring: its localizations are O and its fraction field, whose maximal-ideal completion maps are identities. Apply finite-type stability of G-rings.

The cited finite-type stability proof reduces through quotients/localizations to polynomial extensions and geometrically regular formal fibers. Its characteristic-p formal-fiber lemmas and Cohen structure inputs remain an explicitly recorded source/declaration audit gap; this item does not claim their closure.

items.name: Regularity ascends along a flat map with regular fibers
items.statement: For a flat local homomorphism R→S of Noetherian local rings, if R and S/m_R S are regular then S is regular. Consequently a regular map from a regular Noetherian ring has regular Noetherian target.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4.
proofSteps: The flat local dimension formula gives dim S=dim R+dim(S/m_R S). Lift a minimal generating set of the fiber maximal ideal and adjoin generators of m_R. Their union generates m_S and has exactly dim S elements.

Localize a regular map at a target prime and its contraction to apply the local result. The flat local dimension formula and maximal-ideal generator comparison need their exact supplier audit; L19 alone is only the regularity criterion.

items.name: Regular generic fiber of a completed smooth product
items.statement: In Z55 suppose each B_i[1/π] is smooth over K. Then C[1/π] is a regular Noetherian ring, also when K is imperfect. Flatness over O is not needed for this particular regularity conclusion.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:F0.
proofSteps: The algebraic product P[1/π]=⊗_K B_i[1/π] is smooth by base change and composition, hence regular. Retain this actual smoothness input from U23 for the LLHLM charts.

Z58 and Z57 show P→C is regular; localize at π and use Z59 to obtain regularity of C[1/π]. Z55 identifies this ring with the affinoid completed product. This avoids silently treating the completed tensor as an ordinary tensor or asserting that regular factors have regular product over every field.

items.name: Connected regular Noetherian rings are domains
items.statement: A nonzero connected Noetherian ring B whose localizations at every prime are regular local rings is an integral domain.
items.locator: LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 final paragraph; Tau Ceti connected-domain-stalk theorem and Stacks 00NP
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4.
proofSteps: Z62 supplies domain stalks for Spec B. L58 gives irreducibility. The same domain stalks imply reducedness, as an element vanishing in all prime localizations is zero.

A nonempty reduced affine scheme with irreducible spectrum has a domain coordinate ring. In particular connectedness alone cannot replace regularity: dual numbers are connected and nonreduced; regularity alone cannot replace connectedness: K×K is regular.

items.name: Regular local rings have no zero divisors
items.statement: Every Noetherian regular local ring R is an integral domain.
items.note: Source-level proof plan; no Lean implementation. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4.
proofSteps: Z63 identifies gr_m(R) with a polynomial ring over k. Krull separation L03 gives finite maximal-ideal orders a,b for any nonzero f,g∈R.

Their initial classes are nonzero. Their product in the polynomial graded ring is nonzero, so fg∉m^(a+b+1); in particular fg≠0. This proves the domain conclusion without a purported additive ring map R→gr_m(R).

items.name: One-generic GLn tame inertia has distinct characters
items.statement: Let p be prime, f,n≥1, s=(s_j) in (S_n)^f, and μ a lowest-alcove weight that is 1-deep in every embedding. In formula (2.12), the n characters χ_i of tame inertia are pairwise distinct over a sufficiently large residue field. This is the GLn regularity assertion, with no semisimplicity assumption on an extension to G_K.
items.locator: Definition 2.1.10, Example 2.4.1 and Definition 2.4.3, published PDF33,46–48; LLHLM20 Remark 2.2.4 (rank three)
items.note: Additional source obligation for LocalGaloisDeformationRings; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: Put d=fr where r is the order of s_tau. For distinct indices, the exponent difference D is a sum Σ_{j=0}^{d−1}p^j δ_j. Every δ_j is the difference of two distinct coordinates of a permutation of μ_j+η_j, hence 0<|δ_j|≤p−2. Therefore |D|≤(p−2)(p^d−1)/(p−1)<p^d−1, while D mod p=δ_0 is nonzero. Thus D is not zero modulo p^d−1, the order of the fundamental character. Central shifts cancel; no positivity of the individual coordinates is required.

items.name: Multiplicity-free tame inertia gives semisimplicity
items.statement: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p and F a finite field of characteristic p large enough to split the finite tame inertia image of a continuous finite-dimensional representation ρ:G_K→GL(V). Suppose wild inertia acts trivially and V restricted to inertia is a sum of pairwise distinct one-dimensional characters. Then V is a direct sum of simple F[G_K]-modules, indexed by Frobenius orbits on the inertia characters. Frobenius itself need not act semisimply.
items.locator: Proof adapter for §5.5, published PDF121–125; correct scope of E19
items.note: Additional source obligation for LocalGaloisDeformationRings; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: Finite tame inertia image is cyclic of order prime to p. Its character idempotents split every invariant subspace into intersections with the one-dimensional character spaces. A Frobenius lift permutes those spaces. The sum over each orbit is stable under inertia and Frobenius, hence under the tame image. Any nonzero invariant subspace of this orbit sum contains one character line and consequently every line in the orbit. Thus each orbit sum is simple. No averaging over the Frobenius group and no division by orbit length is used.

items.name: Generic tame residual representations are semisimple
items.statement: For a continuous tame representation ρ:G_K→GL_n(F), if ρ is m-generic in Definition 5.5.1 with m≥1, then ρ is semisimple. The conclusion is stable under a finite splitting-field extension and descends to F.
items.locator: Definition 5.5.1 and the regularity assertion after Definition 2.4.3; published PDF47–48,122
items.note: Additional source obligation for LocalGaloisDeformationRings; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: Restriction to the prime-to-p inertia image is exact and semisimple, so ρ and its G_K-semisimplification have the same inertia constituents with multiplicity. Genericity and K45 make them distinct. Apply K46 after a finite field extension if necessary. An invariant complement descends: its existence is a solvable finite system of linear equations over F (equivariant retraction restricting to identity), whose solvability after field extension implies solvability over F.

items.name: Genericity transfer justifies the tame admissibility argument
items.statement: Under Corollary 5.5.8, let λ_j∈[0,h]^n, let τ have an (h+1)-generic lowest-alcove presentation, and let ρ be tame with R_ρ^(λ,τ) nonzero. After a finite coefficient extension, a characteristic-zero point gives a residual Kisin lattice in Y^[0,h],τ. Corollary 5.5.10 makes ρ 1-generic; hence K47 makes ρ semisimple and Proposition 5.5.7 applies. This supplies the previously missing justification of the semisimple step.
items.note: Additional source obligation for LocalGaloisDeformationRings; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use the fixed-type deformation ring point criterion and lattice comparison to obtain M. The chain K43→K44 is independent of K42: degeneration first replaces any Kisin module by one realizing the residual semisimplification; the height bound then loses at most h from genericity. Apply K47 only after this transfer. Invoke K41 for the original tame ρ, now known semisimple. The residual coefficient extension does not change the inertia-genericity assertion; descent is as in K47.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles partially framed generator bound
items.statement: With the data and Q chosen in A14, there is a continuous surjection R_loc,S,T[[x_1,…,x_g]]→R_SQ^squareT where g=q−Σ_{v∈T,v|p}[F_v+:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 and R_loc,S,T=R_loc,SQ,T. For T=S this is g=q−[F+:Q]n(n−1)/2. All local rings use the fixed multiplier; this is not the unpolarized variable-determinant count.
items.locator: Proposition A.3.3 third conclusion, published PDF193; Thorne Lemma 4.3 and Proposition 4.4, arXiv1107.5989v1 PDF16–18
items.note: Additional source obligation for GlobalGaloisDeformations; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply the relative tangent comparison and the presentation bound in Thorne Lemma 4.3. The augmented dual Selmer term is zero, and ξ(c_v)=−1 annihilates the infinite-place term nΣ(1+ξ(c_v))/2. The remaining expression is g. Lift a generating set of the relative cotangent space and apply complete local Nakayama to obtain the power-series surjection. This proves g is a valid nonnegative bound for the chosen data; arbitrary q without the dual-Selmer lower bound is not allowed.

items.name: Adequacy for polarized finite residual images
items.statement: For a finite subgroup H⊂G_n(F), let H0=H∩G_n^0(F) and let ad V=gl_n(F) with the polarized adjoint action. In Thorne Definition 2.3, H is adequate when H^0(H,ad V)=0, H^1(H0,F)=0, H^1(H,ad V)=0, and for every irreducible F[H]-submodule W⊂ad V there exist h∈H0 and an eigenvalue α of its GL_n component such that tr(e_{h,α}W)≠0; e is the projector to the full generalized α-eigenspace. Work over a finite coefficient field containing the relevant eigenvalues. This G_n definition differs from the GL_n definition using ad^0.
items.locator: Thorne arXiv1107.5989v1 Definition 2.3, PDF6–7; imported by Proposition A.3.3
items.note: Additional source obligation for GlobalGaloisDeformations; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.

uses.how: Provides a nonzero trace functional on a nonzero cohomological image.
Chooses sufficient Taylor–Wiles primes without the stronger big-image hypothesis.

api.name: PolarizedAdequate.toVanishing
api.statement: Export the three cohomology vanishings with the correct H or H0 action and gl_n coefficient module.

api.name: PolarizedAdequate.traceWitness
api.statement: For an irreducible nonzero submodule W of ad V return h,α and a nonzero trace functional on W.

api.name: PolarizedAdequate.ofBig
api.statement: The polarized big-image condition implies adequacy by forgetting eigenvalue multiplicity one, as Thorne Lemma2.4(i).

tests.name: PolarizedAdequate.trivialImage
tests.statement: A trivial subgroup has nonzero adjoint invariants and fails the first adequacy condition.

tests.name: PolarizedAdequate.fullEigenspace
tests.statement: For a scalar Frobenius block of dimension d>1, e_(h,α) projects onto the entire block; choosing one basis line is not invariant and is not the defining trace functional.

tests.name: PolarizedAdequate.bigForget
tests.statement: A valid big-image witness is an adequate witness, with identical cohomology vanishings; the converse is not assumed.

items.name: Trace evaluation kills the auxiliary dual Selmer group
items.statement: In the hypotheses of A14 and for a Taylor–Wiles set Q with the scalar-inertia condition A13, the augmented dual Selmer group is the kernel of H^1_{L^perp,T}(G_{F+,S},ad rbar(1))→⊕_{v∈Q}F given by c↦(tr(e_{Frob_v,α_v}c(Frob_v)))_v. Adequacy and Chebotarev provide a new split prime with nonzero evaluation on any nonzero remaining class, while avoiding a prescribed finite set and enforcing Nv≡1 mod p^N.
items.note: Additional source obligation for GlobalGaloisDeformations; read in continuation codex-c83e7a, 23 September 2026. No implementation claimed.
items.proofOutline: The scalar-inertia local tangent condition has orthogonal complement consisting of unramified classes with trace-zero projection on the selected eigenspace. Apply the local trace pairing and the global restriction exact sequence. On the extension killing ad rbar, a nonzero cohomology class has nonzero invariant image; adequacy gives a nonzero generalized-eigenspace trace. Multiplying a candidate Frobenius element by an element in that kernel makes the trace nonzero if needed. Chebotarev supplies the prime. Iterate on the finite-dimensional dual Selmer space.

items.name: Local-global compatibility at auxiliary parahoric level
items.statement: Assume the Appendix A.4 setting: p>2, F/F+ CM with F+≠Q, all p-adic places split, a unitary group definite at infinity with the chosen integral model away from N, a sufficiently small compact open U, and S containing the p-adic places, primes dividing N and all non-hyperspecial places of U. Fix a dominant algebraic weight λ, WD inertial types τ_v, a stable O-lattice W in ⊗_{v|p}σ(λ_v,τ_v)^*◦ι_v, and the nonzero localized residual Hecke eigensystem with absolutely irreducible rbar|G_F from the Appendix A setup. Fix a Taylor–Wiles datum Q disjoint from S and the associated ideal m_Q away from S∪Q. Put ξ=ε^(1−n)δ_(F/F+)^n. At p use Hodge weights λ_v+η and WD monodromy dominated by τ_v, as required by E33–E34. At U_0(Q) there is a polarized representation r(U_0(Q),W)_mQ:G_{F+,S}→G_n(T_0^pr), with the same corrected deformation datum as A17; in particular it remains unramified at Q. For each allowed split w away from S∪Q, det(1−r|G_F(Frob_w)X)=Σ_{j=0}^n(−1)^j(Nw)^(j(j−1)/2)α_level(T_w^(j))X^j. Here α_level is α_0. Here T_i^pr is the Hecke image on the projected module H_i of A30, and the local assertions use its explicit local-compatibility hypotheses. The unrestricted full-Hecke version of the printed theorem is not established by the cited argument (E38).
items.locator: Theorem A.4.1 second conclusion, published PDF197

items.name: Local-global compatibility at diamond level
items.statement: Assume the Appendix A.4 setting: p>2, F/F+ CM with F+≠Q, all p-adic places split, a unitary group definite at infinity with the chosen integral model away from N, a sufficiently small compact open U, and S containing the p-adic places, primes dividing N and all non-hyperspecial places of U. Fix a dominant algebraic weight λ, WD inertial types τ_v, a stable O-lattice W in ⊗_{v|p}σ(λ_v,τ_v)^*◦ι_v, and the nonzero localized residual Hecke eigensystem with absolutely irreducible rbar|G_F from the Appendix A setup. Fix a Taylor–Wiles datum Q disjoint from S and the associated ideal m_Q away from S∪Q. Put ξ=ε^(1−n)δ_(F/F+)^n. At p use Hodge weights λ_v+η and WD monodromy dominated by τ_v, as required by E33–E34. At U_1(Q) there is a polarized representation r(U_1(Q),W)_mQ:G_{F+,S∪Q}→G_n(T_1^pr) with the same corrected p-adic conditions and, at every v∈Q, the scalar-inertia local condition A13 on the selected summand and an unramified complementary summand. For each allowed split w away from S∪Q, det(1−r|G_F(Frob_w)X)=Σ_{j=0}^n(−1)^j(Nw)^(j(j−1)/2)α_level(T_w^(j))X^j. Here α_level is α_1. The domain allows ramification at Q; it cannot in general be G_{F+,S}. Here T_i^pr is the Hecke image on the projected module H_i of A30, and the local assertions use its explicit local-compatibility hypotheses. The unrestricted full-Hecke version of the printed theorem is not established by the cited argument (E38).

items.name: Uniqueness of the cyclic family monodromy recurrence
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. There is at most one tuple N_j∈Mat_n(R[1/p][[u′]]) with N_j(0)=0 satisfying N_j=E C_j φ(N_(j−1))C_j^−1−N_nabla(C_j)C_j^−1. The j−1 shift is essential.
items.locator: Proposition7.1.3 proof and equation(7.3), published PDF134; arXiv v2 PDF98–99
items.proofOutline: For the difference X of two solutions, X_j=E Ad(C_j)φ(X_(j−1)). Since E and C_j are units/matrices over R[1/p][[u′]], simultaneous divisibility of all X_j by u′^a implies simultaneous divisibility by u′^(pa). Start with a=1; separatedness of formal power series forces every X_j=0. This uses the cyclic system, not an equation with X_j in both slots.

items.name: Integral increment estimate for family monodromy
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. For N_(0,j)=0 and N_(i+1,j)=E C_jφ(N_(i,j−1))C_j^−1−N_nabla(C_j)C_j^−1, one has L^(h−1)(N_(i+1,j)−N_(i,j)) ∈ u′^(p^i)/p^(1+(h−1)(i+1)) · φ^(i+1)(L^h) Mat_n(R[[u′]]) for every i≥0.
items.locator: Equation(7.4) and its induction, published PDF134–135; arXiv v2 PDF99
items.proofOutline: At i=0 the expression is φ(L^h)u′/p^h · C′_j E^h C_j^−1. For the inductive step use L=(E/p)φ(L) to rewrite the increment as E^h/p^(h−1) C_j φ(L^(h−1)(N_(i,j−1)−N_(i−1,j−1)))C_j^−1. The two height-integral matrices preserve integrality, Frobenius multiplies u′-order by p, and the displayed denominator increases by h−1.

items.name: The monodromy limit belongs to the analytic coefficient ring
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. The sequence N_(i,j) converges u′-adically in Mat_n(R[1/p][[u′]]), and L^(h−1)N_(∞,j)∈Mat_n(O_R^rig). Its limit is the unique family operator and is compatible with coefficient maps between rings satisfying the stated hypotheses.
items.proofOutline: The u′-orders p^i tend to infinity. For each fixed analytic chart R[[u′,u′^m/p]][1/p], the exponential numerator order eventually absorbs the denominator p^(1+(h−1)(i+1)) and still leaves u′-order tending to infinity; φ^(i+1)(L^h) is integral on that chart for sufficiently large i. The finitely many initial terms are analytic after a bounded p denominator. Thus the sum lies in every chart, not merely the unrestricted formal power-series ring. Uniqueness glues the eigenbasis charts.

items.name: Ordered Frobenius expansion of the monodromy operator
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. Writing N_(1,j)=L u′(dC_j/du′)C_j^−1, the limit is N_(∞,j)=N_(1,j)+Σ_{i≥1}(∏_{k=0}^{i−1}φ^k(C_(j−k))) φ^i(N_(1,j−i)) (∏_{k=i−1}^{0}φ^k(E C_(j−k)^−1)). The first matrix product is in increasing k order and the second in decreasing k order.
items.proofOutline: Iterate the affine recurrence and telescope successive increments. The Frobenius-twisted linear map is E Ad(C_j)φ with cyclic embedding shift. Expanding its i-th iterate gives the two opposite matrix orders; scalar E factors commute, matrix factors generally do not. G39 justifies passage from finite expansion to the analytic limit.

items.name: Exact descent-removed tail estimate
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. Let (s,μ) be an m-deep lowest-alcove presentation and use A_j,a′_j,s′_or,j,v=u′^e′ of §5.1. Put D_j=Diag((s′_or,j)^−1 a′_j), P_N(A_j)=(-e′v A′_j−[D_j,A_j])(v+p)^h A_j^−1 and Z_(0,j)=−P_N(A_j). The descent-removed identity is p^h Ad((s′_or,j)^−1 u′^(−a′_j))(L^(h−1)N_(∞,j))=−φ(L)^h P_N(A_j)+Σ_{i≥1}φ^(i+1)(L)^h Z_(i,j). Its terms obey Z_(i,j)=p^(1−h) A_j Ad(s_j^−1 v^(μ_j+η_j))(φ(Z_(i−1,j−1)))(v+p)^h A_j^−1 and, for i≥1, Z_(i,j)∈p^(−i(h−1)) v^(1+m(p^i−1)/(p−1)) Mat_n(R[[v+p]]).
items.locator: Equations(7.6),(7.8) and the recursion, published PDF137–139; formula pages inspected visually
items.proofOutline: Remove descent with the conjugating monomial/permutation matrix using (5.4). The derivative of that conjugation contributes [D_j,A_j]; the derivative of v gives e′v. Apply the recurrence to each Frobenius-transformed error. Entrywise exponent bounds use m+1≤〈μ+η,α∨〉≤p−m−1 and the integral height conditions. The exponent is 1+m(1+p+⋯+p^(i−1)), not (m+1)(1+p+⋯+p^(i−1)); this distinction is retained for the coefficient estimates.

items.name: Euler derivatives of the analytic tail have uniform p precision
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. Assume h≥2 and m≥2h−3. At v=−p the error series Σ_{i≥1}φ^(i+1)(L)^h Z_(i,j), together with all its Euler derivatives of orders t≥0, lies in p^(m+2−h)Mat_n(R). The corresponding Euler derivatives of P_N(A_j) vanish modulo (I_nabla∞,p^(m+2−h)) for 0≤t≤h−2.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition7.1.10, equations(7.9),(7.10), published PDF139–140
items.proofOutline: Put D=v d/dv. If F∈v^M R[[v+p]], then D^tF|_(−p)∈p^M R, because Euler differentiation preserves the v^M factor. For k≥1, φ^k(L)(−p) is a p-adic unit, and its positive Euler derivatives are in p^(p−1)Z_p. The ith tail term has valuation at least 1+m(p^i−1)/(p−1)−i(h−1), whose minimum is its i=1 value m+2−h and which tends to infinity. Leibniz gives the same bound for Euler derivatives. Work modulo the saturated true ideal, and recursively divide by the unit φ(L)^h to solve for the derivatives of P_N.
items.note: Exact source obligation in LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels; continuation codex-c83e7a. No implementation claimed.

items.name: Derivative conversion and the lower-triangular precision loss
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. Assume h≥2 and m≥2h−3. For 0≤t≤h−2 and 1≤k,l≤n, the generator (d/dv)^t(v^(−[k>l]) P_N(A_j)_(kl))|_(v=−p) lies in (I_nabla∞,p^(m−(h−1)−t)); hence it lies in (I_nabla∞,p^(m−2h+3)). The expression before evaluation is integral because the lower-triangular entries have a v factor.
items.proofOutline: The Stirling-number identity (v d/dv)^t=Σ_{a≤t}S(t,a)v^a(d/dv)^a has leading coefficient1. Induction on t converts the Euler bound to the ordinary derivative bound m+2−h−t after evaluating v=−p and dividing by p^t in the generic fiber. For k>l put P=vQ and use P^(t)=vQ^(t)+tQ^(t−1), losing at most one further p power. The k≤l entries satisfy the stronger bound and thus the displayed common bound. Finally R/I_nabla∞ is O-flat, so an equality with integral p-power error in its localization descends to the integral quotient.

items.name: Auxiliary Hecke algebra must be restricted to the projector image
items.statement: In the Appendix A.4 global setting, define H_i=pr(S(U_i(Q),W)_mQ) and T_i^pr as the image of the away-from-S∪Q Hecke algebra on H_i, for i=0,1. Assume the raw auxiliary-level Galois representations over the full Hecke algebras, allowing ramification in S∪Q, with the local compatibility and genericity hypotheses of A31–A32. Then the T_0^pr-valued representation is unramified at Q and the T_1^pr-valued representation has local deformation condition A13 at Q. These conclusions follow after projection; no such conclusion over the full auxiliary-level Hecke algebra is inferred.
items.locator: Thorne Theorem6.8 proof, arXiv1107.5989v1 PDF38–39; repair of LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–198; CHT Proposition3.4.4(8) PDF107–109 and patching PDF114–115; EGH Theorem7.2.1 PDF55–56.
items.proofOutline: Thorne first defines H_i,Q and its image Hecke algebra T_i,Q. Proposition5.9 identifies the projected level0 module with the original-level module. Proposition5.12 supplies the scalar-inertia splitting on the projected level1 image algebra. Apply these at each v∈Q; the operators at distinct places commute. The raw global representation and its local compatibility remain explicit global suppliers, rather than being inferred from the projector calculation alone. EGH supplies characteristic-zero representations in the correct arbitrary-rank compact-unitary setting, with Frobenius-semisimplified compatibility away from p and only semisimplified compatibility at p. CHT glues constituent representations over the reduced integral Hecke algebra using its Lemmas2.1.4,2.1.5,2.1.12; those exact descent declarations, the polarization sign and the requisite genericity consequence still need individual supplier checks. CHT3.4.4(8) itself also passes to a selected Hecke image T(Y).
items.note: Exact cited supplier, freshly read in continuation codex-c83e7a. No Lean implementation.

items.name: Parahoric projector compares original-level vectors
items.statement: Let L be a local field of residue cardinality q, with residue characteristic different from the odd coefficient prime p, and q≡1 mod p. Set G=GL_n(L), K=GL_n(O_L), and let P be the standard parahoric for n=n1+n2 (1≤n2≤n). Let O be the coefficient DVR and F its residue field. Let R be a complete local O-algebra with residue F and Π a smooth R[G]-module whose compact-open invariant modules are finite free over O. For each compact open U let R_U be the image of R in End_O(Π^U). Assume Π⊗_O Qpbar is semisimple with generic irreducible constituents and every R_U[1/p] is semisimple. Assume ρ:G_L→GL_n(R_P) is continuous and, at every map R_P→Qpbar and every constituent π generated by the corresponding Π^P specialization, ρ^ss identifies with (r_p(π)^∨(1−n))^ss. Suppose ρbar is unramified and has a Frobenius eigenvalue α with full generalized eigenspace dimension n2. Form the commuting operators V^j (1≤j≤n2), the symmetric-polynomial transforms P_j of the Frobenius characteristic polynomial, and Hensel factorizations P_j=Q_j R_j where R_j mod m_R is a power of X−binom(n2,j)α^j and Q_j at that residue value is a unit. Then pr=∏_j Q_j(V^j) induces an R-linear isomorphism Π^K→pr Π^P. It is the map pr applied to original-level vectors; literal inclusion is not asserted.
items.proofOutline: The selected generalized-eigenvalue factors kill the ramified generic parahoric constituents. Compare characteristic-zero ranks. For integral injectivity reduce to an irreducible mod-p unramified quotient; Thorne Lemma5.10 proves its K-fixed line survives the projector. Hensel coprimality makes the operator invertible on the selected image, but the displayed polynomial operator need not itself be idempotent.
items.note: Exact cited supplier, freshly read in continuation codex-c83e7a. No Lean implementation.

items.name: Projected diamond-level representation has scalar inertia
items.statement: Let L be a local field of residue cardinality q, with residue characteristic different from the odd coefficient prime p, and q≡1 mod p. Set G=GL_n(L), K=GL_n(O_L), and let P be the standard parahoric for n=n1+n2 (1≤n2≤n). Let O be the coefficient DVR and F its residue field. Let R be a complete local O-algebra with residue F and Π a smooth R[G]-module whose compact-open invariant modules are finite free over O. For each compact open U let R_U be the image of R in End_O(Π^U). Assume Π⊗_O Qpbar is semisimple with generic irreducible constituents and every R_U[1/p] is semisimple. Let P1 be the kernel of P→GL_n2(k_L)→k_L^×→k_L^×(p). Assume ρ:G_L→GL_n(R_P1) and the same specialization compatibility as A31, using Π^P1, and let pr be its generalized-eigenspace projector. Put R′=image(R→End_O(pr Π^P1)). Then ρ⊗R′ canonically splits as s⊕ψ, lifting the complementary residual subspace and the selected full α-generalized eigenspace: s is unramified and ψ has scalar tame inertia character χ. For u∈O_L^× the diamond operator V_u on pr Π^P1 equals χ(Art_L(u)).
items.locator: Thorne Proposition5.12 and complete proof, arXiv1107.5989v1 PDF29–30
items.proofOutline: Proposition5.9 and Lemma5.11 leave only unramified or the specified ramified principal-series constituents on the projector image. Their Galois images are abelian. A coprime Hensel factorization of the Frobenius polynomial splits R′^n canonically. The matching Hecke symmetric functions identify the selected eigenvalues, and the unit double-coset operators compute the common inertia character. The image algebra R′ is indispensable in this argument.
items.note: Exact cited supplier, freshly read in continuation codex-c83e7a. No Lean implementation.

items.name: Diamond freeness and augmentation descent
items.statement: In the sufficiently small definite-unitary setting, let V⊂U be normal compact open subgroups equal at p and let Δ=U/V be a finite abelian p-group. For a finite free O coefficient lattice W with the prescribed action, S(V,W) is finite free over O[Δ]. The natural inclusion identifies S(U,W) with S(V,W)^Δ. The trace induces an isomorphism S(V,W)_Δ→S(U,W), so invariants and coinvariants are both identified with the base level through their respective maps. If a commuting spectral projector cuts out a direct summand, its image is also finite free over the local ring O[Δ].
items.locator: Thorne Lemma6.3–6.4 and proofs, arXiv1107.5989v1 PDF33–35; LLHLM23 PDF197–198
items.proofOutline: Prime-to-p stabilizers give exactness of coefficient functors. The Δ-action on the finite double-coset cover is free: any stabilizer maps a prime-to-p group into a p-group. On each orbit the module is a regular O[Δ]-module with the coefficient lattice. Trace gives the coinvariant comparison; inclusion gives the invariant comparison. Hensel spectral separation realizes the selected projector image as a direct summand, and finite projective modules over O[Δ], a local ring, are free. Do not use multiplication by |Δ| as an invertible scalar.
items.note: Exact cited supplier, freshly read in continuation codex-c83e7a. No Lean implementation.

items.name: Maximal-ideal associated graded algebra
items.statement: For a commutative local ring (R,m,k), construct gr_m(R)=⊕_{n≥0} m^n/m^(n+1) as an N-graded commutative k-algebra. Scalar multiplication uses R→k since m annihilates each quotient; multiplication sends the classes of a∈m^i,b∈m^j to ab modulo m^(i+j+1). No choice of a coefficient-field section k→R is required.
items.locator: Stacks 00NO construction in proof; 00IP supplies separation when R is Noetherian.
items.note: Source obligation for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4, shared with its regularity/formal-completion consumers. No matching declaration found in the pinned trees; no implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Changing a by an element of m^(i+1), or b by an element of m^(j+1), changes ab by an element of m^(i+j+1). This defines the graded product; the direct-sum ring laws follow from those of R.
The degree-zero quotient is R/m=k. For any finite generating set x1,…,xe of m, its degree-one classes generate this graded k-algebra, by expanding products of ideal generators.

uses.how: Receives the polynomial map on a minimal set of maximal-ideal generators.
Nonzero initial forms detect the order of a product.

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.degreeZeroEquiv
api.statement: The degree-zero piece is canonically isomorphic to the residue field as an algebra.

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.mk_mul_mk
api.statement: For a∈m^i and b∈m^j, the product of their classes is the class of ab in degree i+j.

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.mk_eq_zero
api.statement: For a∈m^i its degree-i class is zero exactly when a∈m^(i+1).

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.polynomialMap
api.statement: A tuple x1,…,xe∈m defines the graded k-algebra map k[X1,…,Xe]→gr_m(R) sending Xi to the degree-one class of xi.

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.polynomialMap_surjective
api.statement: If the tuple generates m, the polynomial map is surjective.

api.name: MaximalIdealGraded.map
api.statement: A local ring homomorphism R→S sends m_R into m_S and induces a graded ring homomorphism, semilinear over the induced residue-field homomorphism; the construction respects identity and composition.

tests.name: MaximalIdealGraded.field
tests.statement: For a field k all positive-degree pieces vanish and the degree-zero map is the graded algebra equivalence gr_0(k)≅k.

tests.name: MaximalIdealGraded.powerSeriesOneVariable
tests.statement: For R=k[[t]], the degree-n piece has k-basis the class of t^n, and multiplication of these basis elements gives gr_(t)(R)≅k[T].

tests.name: MaximalIdealGraded.dualNumbers
tests.statement: For R=k[ε]/(ε²), gr_(ε)(R)≅k[T]/(T²), with T in degree one; Noetherian locality alone does not make this a polynomial ring.

tests.name: MaximalIdealGraded.mixedCharacteristic
tests.statement: For R=Z_(p), degree n has F_p-basis the class of p^n; the construction uses no impossible ring section F_p→Z_(p).

items.name: Hilbert–Samuel degree equals local dimension
items.statement: For a nonzero Noetherian local ring (R,m,k) of dimension d, n↦length_R(R/m^(n+1)) eventually agrees with a nonzero rational polynomial of degree d. Consequently, for d≥1, dim_k(m^n/m^(n+1)) eventually agrees with a nonzero polynomial of degree d−1; for d=0 these graded pieces eventually vanish.
items.locator: Stacks 00KQ Proposition10.60.9 with 10.59.10; statement and full outer proof read 23 September 2026.
items.note: Source obligation for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4, shared with its regularity/formal-completion consumers. No matching declaration found in the pinned trees; no implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Use the finite-length Hilbert polynomial and its invariance under change of ideal of definition. Bound the degree above by the number of generators of an ideal of definition using monomials.

Induct on dimension, using finite minimal primes and prime avoidance to choose a parameter and lower dimension. In the other direction use a prime chain and multiplication by a nonzero parameter in a domain quotient to lower the Hilbert polynomial degree. These give equality of Krull dimension, polynomial degree and minimal parameter number, as 00KQ.

Take the first finite difference of the cumulative length polynomial. The d=0 case is treated separately; it does not assert a polynomial of degree minus one. Exact suppliers for finite-length Hilbert polynomial existence and the degree-lowering exact sequence remain in analytic-regularity-suppliers.

items.name: A homogeneous relation lowers polynomial-ring growth
items.statement: Let k be a field, d≥1, A=k[X1,…,Xd] with standard grading, and I a homogeneous ideal containing a nonzero homogeneous element f of degree e≥1. For n≥e, dim_k(A/I)_n ≤ binom(n+d−1,d−1)−binom(n−e+d−1,d−1). In particular its eventual Hilbert polynomial, if nonzero, has degree at most d−2 when d≥2; when d=1 the quotient has zero degree-n piece for all n≥e. If I contains a nonzero constant then I=A and all pieces vanish.
items.note: Source obligation for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4, shared with its regularity/formal-completion consumers. No matching declaration found in the pinned trees; no implementation claimed.
proofSteps: Multiplication by f injects A_(n−e) into I_n because the polynomial ring over a field is a domain. Count the degree-n and degree-(n−e) monomial bases and subtract dimensions in the quotient.
The leading terms cancel in the difference of the two binomial polynomials. This argument needs only the stated bound; existence of an eventual polynomial is supplied separately in its applications.

items.name: Associated graded algebra of a regular local ring
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension d, residue field k, and x1,…,xd a minimal generating set of its maximal ideal m. The map k[X1,…,Xd]→gr_m(R) sending Xi to the class of xi is an isomorphism of graded k-algebras. For d=0 this is the residue-field identification and m=0.
items.locator: Stacks 00NO Lemma10.106.1, full proof and its 00KQ/00K3 suppliers read 23 September 2026.
items.note: Source obligation for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4, shared with its regularity/formal-completion consumers. No matching declaration found in the pinned trees; no implementation claimed.
proofSteps: The map is surjective by expansion of products of maximal-ideal generators. Its kernel is homogeneous. If the kernel is nonzero, select a nonzero homogeneous relation. A constant relation is impossible because the degree-zero map is the identity on k.

For d≥1, Z65 gives a strict drop in growth, contradicting Z64, whose graded-piece polynomial has degree d−1. Hence the kernel is zero. For d=0 the empty tuple generates m, so m=0 and the map is already an isomorphism.

routes.reason: Reuse the affine combinatorics candidate already proposed by HE18, HE21, KPZ26 and Zhu17. The finite-root and Coxeter infrastructure at the pins does not supply the extended affine, central-coset, upper-arrow and admissible-pair package.
routes.title: Root systems, Part II: dominance, affine orders and admissible pairs
routes.brief: Reuse RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, preserving its existing HE18/HE21/KPZ/Zhu obligations. Add the extended affine group with central directions, eta-shifted p-dot action, length, Bruhat and upper-arrow orders, regular alcoves, admissibility, reduced products and admissible pairs of LLHLM23 §2.1. Prove the equivalent criteria of Proposition2.1.6 with lambda+eta in both translation bounds, and Corollary2.1.7 modulo X0; supply the reversed restricted-factor version. Opposition is an order equivalence and an anti-homomorphism, not a homomorphism for the same target multiplication. Derive numerical and polynomial genericity transport with the actual loss under small factors. Import finite root data and Coxeter length/order from Root systems (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems); do not duplicate their implementation. Export the affine combinatorics to the modular representation and local-model owners. Test rank one, GL2 central translations, an explicit noncommuting star product and empty nonregular admissible subsets. Suggested file: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems/Affine/AdmissiblePairs.lean. Planets: Admissible pairs; Alcove depth; Affine opposition.

routes.reason: Integral Weyl/dual Weyl modules and the relevant linkage machinery already lie in PA.1. The finite reductive modular owner imports this coefficient-module interface and reconciles it with ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII; characteristic-zero Young symmetrizers are insufficient.
Reuse the LLHLM20 candidate merged in PR2197. Add the all-rank generic finite-group combinatorics without building a second finite reductive representation roadmap.
routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: modular representations and generic Serre weights
routes.brief: Reuse ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups from PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-20. Retain its GL3 lattice/Ext obligations, but put the present all-rank common foundation before those specialized consumers. Import Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, and integral Weyl modules from PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.1, coordinating the common rational-module carrier with ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII. Build good Deligne–Lusztig pairs, sign-normalized characteristic-zero representations, reduction in the Grothendieck group, restricted Serre weights, compatible central lifts, lowest-alcove presentations, outer weights and covering. Prove LLHLM23 Propositions2.3.7–2.3.12 and2.6.2–2.6.6 under their explicit numerical bounds. Correct Proposition2.6.4 to retain tensor W(lambda). The Herzig recipe imports tame inertia/type realization from LocalGaloisDeformationRings and SmoothRepresentationsPartII; it must not assume any global Serre conjecture. Distinguish constituent sets from multiplicities and covering from an arbitrary linkage relation. Test determinant twists in GL2/F11, quotienting by (p-pi)X0, the p19 constituent-depth counterexample and the covering length/equality criterion. Suggested file: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/FiniteReductive/GenericSerreWeights.lean. Planets: Lowest-alcove presentations; Deligne–Lusztig constituents; Herzig weights; Serre-weight covering.

routes.reason: Reuse the existing smooth representation Part II; it already receives depth-zero Deligne–Lusztig types from Newton–Thorne and local type theory from Fintzen/Bushnell–Henniart. These are local K-types, not the modular finite-group reduction theorem.
routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: inertial types and monodromy order
routes.brief: Extend the existing SmoothRepresentationsPartII proposal. Construct Weil–Deligne inertial parameters with their Weil extension and nilpotent operator, the componentwise dominance order on inertia-isotypic Jordan partitions, and the sigma(tau) of LLHLM23 Theorem2.5.4. Split occurrence-implies-dominance, exact-type multiplicity one, and the converse for generic representations; maximal monodromy is required for the final multiplicity-one converse. Prove Proposition2.5.5 for a simultaneous compatible choice of types, using Bushnell–Kutzko, Schneider–Zink and Pyvovarov. Import Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.2), classical LLC from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6, and Deligne–Lusztig representations from ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. Construct the virtual Shotton type when needed by the BM consumer; it may have negative Grothendieck coefficients. Test zero versus maximal monodromy and GL2 principal-series versus Steinberg. Suggested file: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Smooth/InertialTypes.lean. Planets: Inertial type; Monodromy dominance; Type multiplicity one.

routes.reason: L7 owns arbitrary-rank bounded-height Frobenius lattice moduli and their maps to fixed Hodge/inertial-type deformation rings. Add these explicit tame-descent, gauge and residual local-model source obligations there; reserve the true-monodromy polynomial comparison and generic domain theorem for the distinct Part II below. Ordinary lifts use the existing local ordinary infrastructure.

Reuse the KP18/KPZ26/Kisin–Zhou integral local-model proposal for the underlying universal loop spaces, Schubert varieties and coordinates. Differential equations and Galois comparison are not part of this base-geometry route.
routes.title: Geometric Satake and fusion, Part II: integral local models and affine charts
routes.brief: Reuse GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII and its integral Pappas–Zhu base geometry. Add LLHLM23 universal GLn Iwahori over Spec Z[v], completed positive/full/negative loop functors, fpqc Grassmannian, determinant/height bounds, affine-element charts, square-zero Lie splitting and the explicit finite-type chart equations. Retain the functorial Noetherian/completeness assumptions and distinguish sheaf quotients from quotients of R-points. Prove formal etaleness, bounded open immersions, global Schubert orbit projections and the reduced admissible special fibre of the underlying PZ model. These import the affine Weyl owner and ReductiveGroupsPartII parahoric group schemes; no differential local model is automatically reduced. In Proposition3.2.8 allow empty nonpivot coefficient ranges, correcting the printed all-entry nonemptiness assertion. Test n=2, z=1, h=0: the identity matrix exists despite empty off-diagonal ranges. Suggested file: TauCeti/Geometry/LocalModels/UniversalIwahoriCharts.lean. Planets: Universal Iwahori; Negative-loop chart; Pappas–Zhu local model.

routes.reason: Reuse the general deformation/birational, descent and cycle owners for Artinian point criteria, normalization, contraction, generic spreading, Elkik approximation and generic-point-length cycles. The source is a set of precise additional obligations, not a claim that the broad roadmap has already decomposed their proofs. Z45–Z47 supply algebraic connectedness with a rational section without unnecessary normality; Z57–Z59/Z61–Z62 isolate the G-ring/regularity inputs consumed by AdicSpacesPartII. These are source-level additions to the existing owner, with deeper supplier gaps retained.

Complete local coefficient tensors, depth, support and patching algebra are shared infrastructure. U43 now imports the separately extracted original KWII theorem and its domain-only complete-DVR adapter; the affinoid completed product has its own AdicSpacesPartII route. Z15–Z24 refine the R03.1 coefficient-tensor argument. Keep its regular complete-local coordinate lemmas in the early foundational part; do not make this construction depend on later arithmetic patching. Z23 and Z28 import the existing upstream ModularCurves §4D local completion/dimension atom. Only general adic Noetherianity, finite-variable coefficient calculations and coefficient-preserving coordinate adapters are additional R03.1 obligations. Their algebraic dependency graph precedes the arithmetic and modular applications; no whole-roadmap cycle is introduced.
Reuse the Emerton–Gee foundational portion already required by the weight-zero lifting candidate; do not introduce a second representation stack or component labelling.
routes.title: Local Galois deformation rings and their components, Part II: Emerton–Gee stacks and weight-zero lifting geometry
routes.brief: Reuse WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings from PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Its common initial stages own the Noetherian formal stack of etale (phi,Gamma)-modules, algebraic reduced stack, crystalline and potentially crystalline closed formal substacks, versal framed deformation rings, component dimensions and Serre-weight labelling. LLHLM23 consumes those stages before any weight-zero generic-reducedness or automorphy endpoint, so no dependency cycle is introduced. Use Emerton–Gee arXiv:1908.07185v4 with the current author errata: E contains K, universal unramified Frobenius coefficient has prescribed norm, boundary characters require unramified twists, and Theorem5.5.12 uses the replacement induction. Theorem6.5.1 gives component dimension [K:Qp]n(n-1)/2; regular Hodge stacks have total dimension one plus that. Translate the dual/det^(n-1) Serre labels and the opposite Hodge sign used by LLHLM23. Import SchemeAndStackFoundations, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory and LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7. Suggested file: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Galois/EmertonGee/Components.lean. Planets: Galois representation stack; Serre-labelled component; Crystalline versal ring.

routes.reason: Reuse the CEGGPS all-rank patching candidate. The extra source obligation is the exact weak/detectable/minimal functor interface and arbitrary away-from-p-level construction, not another abstract patching roadmap.
routes.title: Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility over Q, Part II: all-rank patching functors and support
routes.brief: Reuse CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity and its CEGGPS construction. Add LLHLM23 Definition6.2.1 as distinct interfaces: nonzero exact weak functor with maximal Cohen–Macaulay type evaluations, weak minimal rank at most one, potentially diagonalizable, detectable on obvious weights, and minimal rank exactly one for a specified type set. Prove Propositions6.2.3–6.2.9 before using generic domain geometry to upgrade weak minimality. Add AppendixA construction for arbitrary away-from-p level: polarized deformation data, adequate auxiliary primes, diamond groups, projectors, ultrafilter modules, exact Pontryagin-dual functor and the support theorem. Keep g=q-[F+:Q]n(n-1)/2. Import GlobalGaloisDeformations G7, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.5/R03.6, PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4 and CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.1–CC.3/CC.8. Share these pre-lattice functor stages with GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. Exactness and MCM do not imply rank one; minimality and detectability remain explicit. Suggested file: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Automorphy/PatchingFunctors.lean. Planets: Weak patching functor; Detectability; Arbitrary-level patching.

routes.reason: The polarized group, local conditions, Selmer tangent complex, framed global ring and adequate Taylor–Wiles primes are already the direction of G7 and the specified deformation layers. This source adds the exact fixed-multiplier tangent and generator formulas, with corrections E22–E24.

Reuse the polarized definite-unitary automorphy-lifting candidate from Boxer–Calegari–Gee, Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis and Newton–Thorne. Add the polynomial-generic domain specialization, rather than creating another automorphy endpoint.
routes.title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: polarized automorphy lifting
routes.brief: Reuse PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. Add LLHLM23 Theorem9.2.1 with every standing CM, split-at-p and unramified-at-p assumption: a finitely ramified polarized lift r, regular potentially crystalline local type (lambda+eta,tau), polynomial-generic tame tau, semisimple residual restrictions at p, adequate residual image over F(zeta_p), zeta_p not in the adjoint fixed field, and a residual RACSDC automorphic lift with matching weight and K-types. The conclusion is automorphy of r with the specified weight and type. The genericity polynomial depends on the weight bounds and coefficient ramification, not on p. Import LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels for domain-or-zero versal rings at semisimple points and the all-rank CEGGPS patching candidate for support. Prove Remark9.2.2 only after the generic Serre-weight theorem supplies change of weight; do not make that weaker initial-weight hypothesis part of the first theorem. Preserve existing Thorne/BLGGT targets and normalization adapters. Suggested file: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Automorphy/GenericLocalDomains.lean. Planets: Generic local domain; Polarized modularity lifting.

routes.reason: Reuse and broaden the pre-lattice common stages of the LLHLM20 candidate to the all-rank generic Breuil–Mezard/Serre theory. Keep its specialized GL3 integral-lattice endpoint separate; the legacy candidate id does not restrict the shared foundation to rank three.
routes.title: Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: generic Breuil–Mézard, Serre weights and GL3 lattices
routes.brief: Reuse GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices from LLHLM20, broadening its common pre-lattice foundation to LLHLM23 §§8–9 in arbitrary rank; retain its rank-three lattice conclusions with their own stronger hypotheses. Import finite-group constituents and covering from ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups, representation stack components from WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings, local monodromy comparisons from LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels, generic-point-length cycles from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5, and the exact weak/minimal functors from the existing all-rank CEGGPS patching candidate. Build geometric and versal BM interfaces, component-meeting testing sets, irrelevant weights, relative spanning systems, truncation idempotents, rational inversion and effectivity descent. Theorem8.3.5 needs rank-one minimal patching and component-meeting points. Theorem8.4.10 gives canonical supported generic cycles via semisimple pullbacks; polynomial-type equations alone have uniqueness only in the stronger Proposition8.6.5 range. Corollary8.5.2 allows wild residual representations with sufficiently generic semisimplification, and virtual tame WD types with signed coefficients; it does not extend the tame domain theorem. For finite Lambda containing zero retain all shifted polynomial and depth bounds. Prove the unit leading coefficient, triangular integral basis and the corrected defect recursion excluding the target weight. Finally prove Theorem9.1.6 for automorphic residual definite-unitary data, F+ not Q, p not dividing 2n, split unramified p-places, adequate image over F(zeta_p), and tame polynomial-generic local parameters, allowing arbitrary away-from-p level. Separate general conjectures from these proved cases. Order common patching and generic BM before GL3 lattice consumers to avoid a globalization/lattice cycle. Suggested files: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Galois/GenericBreuilMezard.lean and TauCeti/NumberTheory/Automorphy/GenericSerreWeights.lean. Planets: Breuil–Mézard cycle; Minimal patching; Generic Serre weights; Defect recursion.

routes.reason: L7 supplies bounded-height lattices and fixed-type rings; the new theorem family is the comparison with differential local models, their generic unibranchness, component geometry and true-monodromy approximation. This differs from the existing unrestricted-ring normality and rank-two Barsotti–Tate candidates.
routes.title: Local Galois deformation rings and their components, Part II: monodromy local models and generic components
routes.brief: Build on LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, importing its bounded-height Kisin stacks, tame descent, gauge bases and fixed-type lifting rings. Import integral PZ/loop geometry from GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, affine admissibility from RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure, modular finite-group theory from ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups, scheme normalization/Elkik lemmas from SchemeAndStackFoundations, completed-tensor algebra from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra and the common Emerton–Gee foundation from WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Construct the universal differential locus, naive intersections and flat closures separately. Prove flag generic fibres, contracting chart actions, spreading of normality and product unibranchness with the ramification-index bound; give the Type A affine Springer fixed-point input its own source-bound leaf. Develop residual differential cells, intrinsic C_(w,omega), Serre labels and torus lifts with all genericity bounds, including the corrected Theorem4.6.2 bound max(2n,h_lambda+n-1). Construct analytic monodromy, the convergent recurrence, true flat-closure ideal and basis-dependent truncated ideal; prove the precision containment before Elkik comparison. The exact endpoint is Theorem7.3.2 for regular lambda_j in [0,h]^n and unramified local fields: numerical N_sing gives a noncanonical closed immersion, and a nonzero integral polynomial depending on the Hodge set and coefficient ramification gives the completed regular chart isomorphism and domain-or-zero versal rings at semisimple residual points. Do not claim global canonical gluing or wild-point domains. Prove Theorem7.4.2 component support under max{2(h+1),4n+h}-depth and Proposition7.4.7 with its separate fixed-point polynomial hypothesis. Include the rank-three AppendixB chart, localized equations, normalization and dense branching locus as concrete tests; uniform CAS identities need certificates. Suggested files: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Galois/LocalModels/Differential.lean, Monodromy.lean and GenericComparison.lean. Planets: Differential local model; True monodromy; Generic local-model comparison; Serre-labelled component; Rank-three normalization. Theorem3.7.1 uses two distinct tensor topologies: import the complete-local domain adapter from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra and the completed affinoid product from AdicSpacesPartII R0/F0. Elkik precision is now extracted through Z03–Z07, retaining N=2r+1 and the t^(m−r) agreement.

claudeCc442dc5Continuation.handChecks: Small cases behind the tests were checked by hand: GL2 Adm((1,0)) and Adm((2,0)) (3 and 5 elements, 2 and 4 regular), Ω for GL2, star anti-multiplicativity, depth and P1-genericity at p=7, the dot action, GL2 Herzig involution R(Sym^r⊗det^b)=Sym^{p−2−r}⊗det^{r+b+1−p} with R² a twist, W?/W_obv counts 2/2 for GL2 and 9/6 for GL3 via Proposition 2.6.2, tame characters τ(s,μ) for GL2 and the class (λ+η)|_Z of w̃(ρ̄,τ). api: Form H from the chosen finite polynomial presentation and its conductor-weighted minors.
The image of an admissible H_B under coefficient base change lies in the new conductor-weighted Jacobian ideal.
Evaluate H_B under the polynomial-evaluation map; a power-membership witness is recorded as a finite expression when supplied.
The complement of V(H) in Spec(B) is the smooth locus; distinguish the full H from a smaller chosen witness ideal.
Export a concrete finite identity v^r=h+j with h∈H and j∈J for use after all base changes.
unitTests: For J=(f), the nonempty one-row contribution is the gradient ideal; keep the empty-row annihilator contribution separate if that convention is used.

api: A finite scalar extension preserves the finite-extension connectedness condition.
It suffices to test a cofinal collection of finite field extensions; connectedness descends along further field extension.
For every finite extension, idempotents are only zero and one.
The completed tensor product preserves this condition once the affinoid fiber comparison is established.
unitTests: K itself satisfies the condition.
A nontrivial finite separable field extension of K is connected but not geometrically connected after a splitting extension.

api: Form q^n and contract along R→R[1/π]; identify membership with some π-power multiple in P^n.
For m≤n construct Q_n→Q_m from J_n⊂J_m; prove identity and composition, compatibility of augmentations to O, and J_1=P.
Multiplication by π on Q_n is injective, by saturation; combine with DVR factorization for torsionfreeness.
A local O-algebra map commuting with the chosen retractions carries J_n into J_n and induces a compatible map of quotient systems. No arbitrary base-change equality is asserted.
Construct the canonical Q_n⊗_O K ≅ A/q^n, compatible in n; see Z18.
Under the given Noetherian hypotheses Q_n is finite free over O by Z17; do not choose bases functorially.
unitTests: For R=O[[x]], ξ(x)=0, J_n=(x^n), Q_n has basis 1,x,…,x^(n−1).
For R=O[[x,y]]/(πy−x²), ξ(x)=ξ(y)=0, y∈J_2 but y∉P²; Q_n has basis y^j,xy^j of weights 2j,2j+1<n.
For R=O[[x]]/(πx), every J_n=(x); the separated-jet assertion requires more than a retraction.
